REPRODUCED (main, 9.0); 8.6 has no abstract lists

  • Platform generic
  • Tested reporter's script with own main tcltest (9.1, wt-a1) and tcl9.0 tip tcltest; identical output to the report on both.
  • Cause generic/tclListObj.c:TclListObjAppendElements (used by Tcl_ListObjAppendElement, compiled lappend in procs, and the single-element-at-end shortcut of Tcl_LinsertObjCmd) goes straight to TclListObjGetRep, which converts the abstract list; only Tcl_ListObjReplace consults the type's replaceProc.
  • Prototype prototypes/0c82728f85.patch (56 lines, test abstractlist-bug-0c82728f85). In TclListObjAppendElements, if the object has replaceProc and lengthProc, delegate to TclObjTypeReplace(interp, toObj, length, 0, elemCount, elemObjv). Fixes all three cases; abstractlist/list*/lappend/linsert/lseq tests pass (11700 tests, 0 failed). Design question (whether append should honour the hook) still for the maintainers; applies to 9.0 as well.
  • Suggested ticket comment TclListObjAppendElements() does not check for a replaceProc, unlike Tcl_ListObjReplace(), so lappend in a proc and single-element "linsert ... end" convert the abstract list. Proposed fix: delegate to the replaceProc there (patch with test abstractlist-bug-0c82728f85).

🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

b989a6a0e0.patch: VERIFIED. It is over the size guideline, the table should be produced by tools/uniParse.tcl, and the glob path and backrefs stay ToLower-only. Also note that i now matches U+0131/U+0130 under -nocase (the same as Python's re.IGNORECASE, but string equal -nocase does not do this).

  • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71)
  • Before work-a3/vb989.tcl against "K" -> ^k$=1 ^k{1}$=0 ^k+$=0 ^[k]$=0 ^[k]+$=0 ^[a-z]$=0; regexp -nocase {^K+$} K = 0; ſ (U+017F) vs ^[s]$/^s+$ = 0
  • Patch applied cleanly (80 changed lines, about 15 of them the generated table). I regenerated the 53-entry table from the tip's case tables (work-a3/vb989gen.tcl: c with fold=lower(upper(c)) not in {fold, upper, title}), and it matches the patch exactly.
  • After all the ticket forms and [a-z] -> 1; {^K+$} vs K -> 1; ſ vs [s]/s+ -> 1. As the triage said, bare ^s$ vs ſ is still 0 (glob path, ToLower only). Tests regexp (275/0 failed), regexpComp, reg (1072/0), string, utf: 0 failed
  • Test existing regexp-33.1 and 33.2 (from the patch) fail on the unpatched tip / pass after
Full verdict

REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.5)

  • Platform generic
  • Tested own main build, 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.5.19 — same results on all. Also asymmetric: regexp -nocase {^K$} K is 0 while it matches k.
  • Cause generic/regc_locale.c:allcases()/range() build the -nocase set from only ToLower/ToUpper/ToTitle of the pattern char, so {k,K} never gets U+212A (whose lower is k, but nothing maps back to it). Bare ^k$ "works" only because the compiler turns it into a string match -nocase (TclReToGlob), which compares ToLower of both sides. A scan of the Tcl case tables finds 53 such one-way mappings (U+212A, U+212B, U+2126, U+017F, U+0130/0131, U+03C2, U+1C80–1C88, U+2C6x, U+A7xx, ...).
  • Prototype prototypes/b989a6a0e0.patch (175 lines incl. a generated 53-entry table and tests regexp-33.1/33.2; bigger than the "small" limit). Adds a static {fold, other} table (fold = ToLower(ToUpper(c))) to regc_locale.c; allcases() and range() add the other members of the class. Fixes all forms in the report and ranges like [a-z]; reg*/string* tests pass (3273, 0 failed). A proper fix should generate the table in tools/uniParse.tcl along with tclUniData.c. Remaining inconsistency: the glob path still uses ToLower only, so bare ^s$ does not match U+017F while [s] now does; backrefs (casecmp) are also ToLower only.
  • Suggested ticket comment The regexp -nocase sets come from ToLower/ToUpper/ToTitle of the pattern char only, so chars like U+212A whose lowercase is k are not reached from k; bare ^k$ matches only because it is compiled to string match. Proposed fix: add the missing case counterparts (53 in the current tables) in regc_locale.c allcases()/range(); prototype with tests regexp-33.*.

  • 💬 2026-10-16 serhiy.storchaka: Reproduced on 9.0 and main with a local server that closes idle keep-alive connections: http::CheckEof closes the idle socket after geturl has chosen to reuse it but before http::OpenSocket runs, so the reuse path reads the removed socketWrState element. Proposed fix in branch http-keepalive-reuse-closed: OpenSocket opens a new connection in that case. Test http-4.19. It also fixes 3764f4e81f.
Full verdict

REPRODUCED (main, 9.0); not in 8.6 (http 2.9.9)

  • Platform generic
  • Tested main (own build, http 2.10.3), 9.0.5 (http 2.10.2), 8.6.18 (http 2.9.9), with a localhost server that keeps the connection alive but closes it while the client is idle (work-a4/s/05b_server.tcl, 05b_client.tcl). Every reuse after a server close fails on 9.x.
  • Cause library/http/http.tcl: geturl (PreparePersistentConnection path) decides to reuse the persistent socket and schedules OpenSocket with after idle; in http::wait's vwait the pending readable event runs CheckEof -> CloseSocket -> CloseQueuedQueries -> Unset, which removes socketMapping/socketWrState for the connection. OpenSocket then still takes the reusing branch, and ScheduleRequest reads the unset socketWrState($connId).
  • Prototype prototypes/05b158ed56.patch (79 lines, test http-4.19.*): in OpenSocket, if $state(reusing) but socketMapping($connId) no longer exists, switch to a fresh placeholder, start the timeout timer and call PreparePersistentConnection, i.e. open a new connection. The repro passes; http*.test passes.
  • Suggested ticket comment Reproduced on 9.0 and main with a local server that closes idle keep-alive connections. The idle socket is closed by http::CheckEof after geturl has chosen to reuse it but before http::OpenSocket runs, so the reuse path reads the removed socketWrState element. Prototype: open a new connection in OpenSocket in that case; test http-4.19.

e27c3246c3.patch: VERIFIED (affects every Win32 API call on Windows, not run there)

  • Patch applied cleanly (tclTest.c hunks offset up to 142 lines; 90 changed lines, over the size limit as the triage said: ~15 in tclUtf.c)
  • After {0041 FFFD 0042} {FFFD FFFD FFFD} {FFFD 0042 FFFD FFFD 0042 FFFD FFFD 0042} {FFFD FFFD FFFD FFFD}; tests utf 401/0 failed, encoding 230/0, string 1411/0, stringObj 85/0, icu 58/0, cmdIL 164/0, format 271/0, scan 184/0, regexp 273/0; doc/Utf.3 paragraph renders correctly. TclNumUtfChars also calls Tcl_UtfToChar16 but only uses the byte count, which is unchanged
  • Test existing utf-27.2 fails before (with the test command) / passes after; utf-27.1 (valid input) passes on both
Full verdict

REPRODUCED (main, 9.0; 8.6 not applicable — Tcl 8 keeps cp1252/Latin-1 fallback by design)

  • Platform generic (mainly matters on Windows, where Tcl_UtfToWCharDString = Tcl_UtfToChar16DString feeds every Win32 API call)
  • Tested main build with a new testutftochar16 test command. Before the patch, A\x80B gives 0041 0080 0042; in the middle of a string the same \x80 gives U+20AC via cp1252, so the result changes with the position. Naked 0xA0–0xBF and broken lead bytes come out as themselves. 9.0 has the same code (by reading).
  • Cause generic/tclUtf.c Tcl_UtfToChar16 maps 0x80–0x9F through the cp1252 table and every other invalid byte to itself. The tail loop of Tcl_UtfToChar16DString also stores incomplete sequences as UCHAR(*p++). tclIcu.c already avoids Tcl_UtfToChar16DString for this reason (comment there).
  • Prototype prototypes/e27c3246c3.patch (90 changed lines, over the size limit: about 15 in tclUtf.c, the rest is the test command testutftochar16 in tclTest.c, a doc/Utf.3 paragraph for Tcl_UtfToChar16, and tests utf-27.1/27.2). Invalid bytes become U+FFFD. The surrogate-pair path (high surrogate from the 4-byte lead, low surrogate from the trail bytes) and the C0 80 NUL are kept. utf/encoding/string/stringObj/icu/cmdIL tests pass. Tcl_UtfToUniChar(DString) keeps cp1252 (not touched; changing it would affect all string handling).
  • Suggested ticket comment Confirmed on main and 9.0. Proposed patch makes Tcl_UtfToChar16 and the tail of Tcl_UtfToChar16DString store U+FFFD for invalid or incomplete sequences instead of cp1252 / the raw byte, with a testutftochar16 test command and tests utf-27.*. This is a visible behaviour change for Windows API strings, so it probably needs a TIP or at least a changes.md entry.

  • Platform generic
  • Tested small stubs extension calling Tcl_RegisterConfig twice for the same package (work-a2/rc): after the 2nd call demopkg::pkgconfig list fails with "package not known" on main (own build), 9.0 tip, 8.6 tip.
  • Cause generic/tclConfig.c:Tcl_RegisterConfig: the merged package dict is put into the database first, then Tcl_CreateObjCommand replaces the old ::pkg::pkgconfig, whose QueryConfigDelete removes that package entry (and frees the merged dict).
  • Prototype prototypes/67769bcad3.patch (58 lines incl. new testregisterconfig command in tclTest.c, test pkgconfig-3.1; the fix itself is 5 lines: hold a reference to the dict and re-put it after the command is created).   • Suggested ticket comment Confirmed in 8.6, 9.0 and main: replacing the query command runs QueryConfigDelete, which removes the just-merged package dict. Proposed fix: keep a reference and put the dict back after Tcl_CreateObjCommand, with a test (pkgconfig-3.1 via a new testregisterconfig command).

  • Platform generic
  • Tested main built with -DPURIFY under valgrind, TCL_FINALIZE_ON_EXIT=1, with a small extension (work-a4/s/idleleak.c) that calls Tcl_DoWhenIdle 100 times and exits: 3,200 bytes in 100 blocks definitely/indirectly lost from Tcl_DoWhenIdle; none with the prototype.   • Tested code inspection; Unix has no equivalent (no reserved device names)
  • Cause win/tclWinFile.c NativeAccess: file exists (F_OK) only calls GetFileAttributesW. For bare reserved names comN (N=1..9, recognised by WinIsReserved) Windows reports attributes whether or not the device exists; for \\.\comN device paths GetFileAttributesW fails, so exists/readable/writable return 0. file type goes through NativeStat, which opens the device with CreateFileW and therefore reflects reality.

Full verdict

REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6)

  • Platform generic
  • Tested the attached switch_test.tcl on main/9.0.5/8.6.18 (the 3/4/5-arg cases give wrong lines). Smaller repro without traces: a proc whose body is not a literal, with both switches called as $sw so neither is compiled inline. info frame 0 in the inner arms gives 3 3 3 2 instead of 2 2 2 2.
  • Cause generic/tclCmdMZ.c Tcl_SwitchObjCmd. When the pattern/body list is split and no source lines are known, it fills ctxPtr->line with -1 for the list elements, but the frame keeps type TCL_LOCATION_BC (the outer arm body was compiled with relative counting). TclInitCompileEnv then calls TclGetSrcInfoForPc again on that BC invoker, which puts back the word lines of the switch command itself. The list index j of the body is then looked up in the switch's argument words. Bodies with j < number of switch words get a wrong line, so the number of bad arms grows with the number of options, as reported.
  • Prototype prototypes/5d5b105228.patch (46 changed lines, test switch-20.1). In that branch it changes the frame type from BC to TCL_LOCATION_EVAL, so the compiler counts lines relatively. The test also checks that absolute lines in a sourced literal body do not change. switch/info tests pass; the attached script then prints all "ok". Applies to 9.0 and 8.6 with fuzz.
  • Suggested ticket comment Cause: when switch splits its body list in a BC frame without source info, TclInitCompileEnv fetches the switch command's own word lines again (TclGetSrcInfoForPc) and indexes them with the list position of the arm. Proposed fix: mark the frame as EVAL in that case; test switch-20.1.

  • Platform build (unix)
  • Tested own main checkout with Thread trunk unpacked into pkgs/ (from thread.fossil), out-of-tree build. ../tcl9.1/unix/configure --srcdir=../tcl9.1/unix: make fails in configure-packages with "configure: error: cannot find sources () in ../tcl9.1/unix". Without --srcdir it builds. (The reporter's --srcdir=../tcl9.0.2, i.e. the top dir rather than unix/, is a user error: config.status cannot find ../unix/Makefile.in.)
  • Cause unix/configure.ac: PKG_CFG_ARGS="$ac_configure_args ..." forwards Tcl's own --srcdir to each package's configure, so it looks for its sources in Tcl's unix dir. The --with-tcl=../.. relative path is not the problem; the package configure is run via the absolute $(TCL_SRC_DIR)/pkgs/<pkg>/configure.
  • Prototype prototypes/17ffc49790.patch (configure.ac 4 lines + regenerated configure): strip --srcdir=X / --srcdir X from PKG_CFG_ARGS. Verified: both forms then build pkgs/thread. (make install of my Thread trunk tarball then fails for an unrelated reason: the fossil tarball lacks tclconfig/install-sh.)
  • Suggested ticket comment The failure comes from Tcl's own --srcdir being forwarded to the bundled packages' configure via PKG_CFG_ARGS. Proposed fix: drop --srcdir from PKG_CFG_ARGS; the packages find their sources from the absolute path of their configure script. Note --srcdir must point to the unix directory, not the top of the source tree.

Full verdict

REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.5, 8.4)

  • Platform generic
  • Tested reporter's script on wt-a3 main, 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.5.19, 8.4.20 — all fail with can not find channel named "stdout"; with any prior channel op in the parent all work.
  • Cause generic/tclIO.c:GetChannelTable registers stdin/stdout/stderr lazily on an interp's first channel operation. If the child does it first, it holds the only reference, so close stdout there really closes the thread's stdout; the parent later finds no std channel.
  • Prototype prototypes/fb9acd64a5.patch (65 lines, test interp-41.1): new internal TclInitChannelTable(), called by ChildCreate (tclInterp.c) for the parent before the child is created, so the parent always holds its own reference (same as the "puts start" case). interp/io*/chan*/safe* tests pass. Probably not enough for the related 5338d8e82.
  • Suggested ticket comment The parent registers the std channels only on its first channel operation, so a child that closes stdout first drops the last reference. Proposed fix: initialise the parent's channel table when creating a child; test interp-41.1.

Open ticket 0b3595a819 · 21. [namespace] · filed 2025-03-29

Full verdict

REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6)

  • Platform generic
  • Tested reporter's PoC (time instead of timerate) on wt-a3 main, 9.0.5, 8.6.18: chain of 100 imports works (2–4 us/call), chains of 1000 and 5000 fail with "too many nested evaluations (infinite loop?)".
  • Cause an imported command is a forwarding command (tclNamesp.c InvokeImportedNRCmd) that calls the next ImportedCmdData->realCmdPtr, which can itself be an import, so each call walks the whole chain with one NRE level per link (counted against the recursion limit). TclGetOriginalCommand already resolves the chain, but invocation does not use it.
  • Prototype none (sebres has a rewrite in his fork, to be done together with 62dafd9c53; changing import resolution/ownership is beyond a small fix).
  • Suggested ticket comment Still present in main, 9.0 and 8.6 (chain of 1000 imports gives "too many nested evaluations"). Waiting for the backport of the fork's rewrite.

  • Suggested ticket comment Reproduced on Linux too: -force only makes the top-level directory writable (DoRemoveDirectory in unix/tclUnixFCmd.c), not read-only subdirectories, contrary to file.n. Proposed fix: make read-only subdirectories writable during the traversal; test fCmd-5.13.

  • Platform generic
  • Tested reporter's script (single thread, 40 rounds of 1M array set/get) on main -O2, main -O2 -DPURIFY, 8.6.18
  • Cause generic/tclThreadAlloc.c: the per-thread bucket/object caches are plain LIFO lists, so after many alloc/free cycles consecutive allocations are scattered in memory. Full verdict

REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6; Release builds with the threaded allocator, long DLL paths only)

  • Platform Windows
  • Tested code reading only; Unix uses dlopen/dlerror and is not affected. Repro script: win/66aa81c90a.tcl with a prebuilt x86_64 mingw test DLL win/66aa81c90a/needsdep.dll (it imports a missing missingdep66aa.dll). The script loads it from a short and from a long (>100 chars) path.
  • Cause win/tclWinLoad.c TclpDlopen reads GetLastError() for the second LoadLibraryExW only after Tcl_DStringFree(&ds). When the native path is longer than the DString static buffer, the free goes through Tcl's allocator. The threaded allocator (default in 9.0; not in 8.6 MSVC builds) calls TlsGetValue, which sets the last error to 0. ERROR_SUCCESS then hits the default: case and gives "No error". This explains why Jan's short ./tcl9memorymoduletest.dll got the correct message and Harald's long C:/... path did not. The code is the same in 8.6, so 8.6 builds with the threaded allocator would show it too.
  • Prototype prototypes/66aa81c90a.patch (11 changed lines; saves the second LoadLibraryExW error before Tcl_DStringFree). Not compiled or tested on Windows.
  • Suggested ticket comment Probable cause: TclpDlopen calls GetLastError() after Tcl_DStringFree; for paths that do not fit the DString static buffer the free goes through the threaded allocator (TlsGetValue), which clears the last error, so it reads 0 = "No error". Proposed patch saves the error right after LoadLibraryExW; it still needs to be checked on Windows.
Windows VM, run 3

  • Platform generic

  • Cause generic/tclPkg.c PkgRequireCoreStep1 runs the package unknown script while the requiring package's name is on top of the tclPkgFiles stack. tclPkgUnknown itself uses source -nopkg, but plain source calls inside pkgIndex.tcl (tcllib's top-level index) are recorded via TclPkgFileSeen, so every nested failed require adds all those pkgIndex.tcl files. Jan's idea (remember the pkgIndex.tcl in the ifneeded data) is already implemented (30f95df8b0); this is the remaining leak.
  • Prototype prototypes/209fd9adce.patch (48 changed lines, 15 in C, test package-bug-209fd9adce): hide the names stack (set to NULL) while the unknown script runs, restore in PkgRequireCoreStep2, as source -nopkg does. package.test, pkgMkIndex.test pass.
  • Suggested ticket comment Still present: tclPkgUnknown uses <tt>source -nopkg</tt>, but plain <tt>source</tt> calls inside pkgIndex.tcl (e.g. tcllib's top-level index) run during a nested <tt>package unknown</tt> are recorded for the package being loaded. Proposed fix: hide the package-name stack while the <tt>package unknown</tt> script runs (patch + test package-bug-209fd9adce available).

Open ticket b5a02c5390 · 29. http Package · filed 2024-07-16

🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

b5a02c5390.patch: VERIFIED

  • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71)
  • Before the patch's test used as repro with the library change stashed: TCL_LIBRARY=wt-a2/library ./tcltest ../tests/http.test -match 'http-4.20*' -> both thread levels FAILED with {{can't read "state(socketinfo)": no such element in array}} {} 1 sock... (bgerror after cleanup, token still exists, socket leaked)
  • Patch applied with offset +7 in http.test (re-saved, 39 changed lines, content unchanged)
  • After http.test: 156 total, 150 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed; http11.test: 98 total, 86 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed (httpProxy/httpPipeline not run, per rules)
  • Test existing http-4.20.* fails before / passes after
Full verdict

REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6)

  • Platform generic
  • Tested localhost, no TLS needed (work-a4/s/b5a.tcl): geturl -command ... -keepalive 0, update idletasks (socket opened, connect pending), http::cleanup, then enter the event loop. The writable handler still calls http::Connect on the cleaned-up token, which raises a bgerror (8.6.18/http 2.9.9: can't read "state(sock)", as in the ticket; 9.0.5 and main: can't read "state(socketinfo)" from Finish, because Connect's eof check is now caught). The socket also leaks. With -keepalive 1 the same bgerror happens on 9.0.
  • Cause library/http/http.tcl:http::cleanup only cancels timers/coroutines and unsets the state array. For a transaction still in progress it leaves the socket open and its fileevent handlers pointing at the dead token. Harald's proposed guard in Connect would hide the error, but the socket and its handlers would still leak.
  • Prototype prototypes/b5a02c5390.patch (72 lines, test http-4.20.*): in http::cleanup, if state(status) is still "" and a socket exists, unset state(-command) (no user callback from cleanup) and catch {reset $token}, which closes or releases the socket before the state is unset. The repro is clean (no bgerror, no leaked channel); the http*.test files pass; http-4.20 fails on unpatched 9.0. Side note, not addressed: with -keepalive 1 a reset in the middle of a request leaves the socket in socketMapping, so it may be reused with a half-finished exchange.
  • Suggested ticket comment Reproduced without TLS: cleanup while the socket is still connecting leaves the writable handler (http::Connect) and the socket behind, giving this bgerror on 8.6 and a similar one (state(socketinfo)) on 9.0/main. Proposed fix: http::cleanup resets an unfinished transaction (without calling -command) instead of guarding Connect only; test http-4.20.

  • Tested reporter's script with testbumpinterpepoch on wt-a3/unix/tcltest (main), tcl9.0 and tcl8.6 tip tcltest: first run after the bump prints "line 2" instead of "line 4" for info frame 0; second run is correct.

  • Suggested ticket comment Still reproducible in main, 9.0, 8.6. Cause: instStartCmdFailed re-evaluates the command text as a new string without location info. Branch bug-31fd84270644f67d has the test only.

    • Platform build/docs

    ⬜89fbf1f86e2023Unclean memory handlingREPRODUCED (main; 8.6 per ticket comments, not rebuilt with PURIFY here)

    Open ticket 89fbf1f86e · 41. Memory Allocation · filed 2023-08-31

    Full verdict

    REPRODUCED (main; 8.6 per ticket comments, not rebuilt with PURIFY here)

    • Platform generic
    • Tested main -O2 -DPURIFY build under valgrind; 2-line script set a 0; exit $a already gives 144 bytes definitely lost, if 1 {exit $a} adds CFWord blocks from TclArgumentEnter
    • Cause [exit] calls Tcl_Exit -> Tcl_Finalize -> FreeMainInterp and never returns to the C frames that hold references: TclEvalEx's substituted word objects (TclSubstTokens) and CFWord records (TclArgumentEnter/TclArgumentRelease), and Tcl_FSEvalFileEx's normalized path. Once the main interp's tables are freed, these become unreachable and valgrind reports them as definitely lost. 8.5 showed no such report because it did not delete the main interp at exit, so the same blocks stayed "still reachable". The leak is bounded (once per process) and only exists in exit paths.
    • Prototype none (fixing it needs [exit] to unwind the C stack to Tcl_Main before finalizing, which changes how exit behaves; alternatively add these frames to tools/valgrind_suppress)
    • Suggested ticket comment Still on main: set a 0; exit $a in a script file is enough with a PURIFY build. The lost blocks are owned by C frames (TclEvalEx, Tcl_FSEvalFileEx) that Tcl_Exit never returns to, so they leak once per process, at exit. A real fix means making &#91;exit&#93; unwind to Tcl_Main before Tcl_Finalize; a cheap option is adding these frames to tools/valgrind_suppress.

    ⬜5338d8e82f2023Closing the std* channels and opening replacements sometimes doesn't register the std* channel name in interpsREPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.7b1, 8.6, 8.5). The behaviour follows from the documented design (NOT-A-BUG, doc clarification at most).

    Open ticket 5338d8e82f · 25. Channel System · filed 2023-05-04

    Full verdict

    REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.7b1, 8.6, 8.5). The behaviour follows from the documented design (NOT-A-BUG, doc clarification at most).

    • Platform generic
    • Tested reporter's script with a file instead of the tty (work-a4/s/std.tcl) on main, 9.0.5, 8.7b1, 8.6.18, 8.5.19: all give can not find channel named "stdout".
    • Cause the standard channels are per thread (tclIO.c tsdPtr->stdoutChannel), and each interp that uses them registers its own reference. The parent's puts registers stdout in the parent, so close stdout in the child only drops the child's reference. The thread-level channel stays open, the stdout slot is not emptied, and Tcl_CreateChannel makes the new file an ordinary fileN. Without the parent's puts the child holds the last reference, the slot is emptied, and the new channel becomes stdout (StdChannels.3, "Re-initialization"), but then for every interp in the thread, the parent included.
    • Prototype none (by design; per-interp std channels would be a redesign)
    • Suggested ticket comment Standard channels are per thread, not per interp. close stdout in a child only unregisters it there while the parent still holds it, so the slot is not empty and the next opened channel does not become stdout (see StdChannels.3, "Re-initialization of Tcl standard channels"). To redirect a child's output, give the child its own channel (e.g. open it in the child and use interp alias/a puts wrapper), or close stdout in all interps of the thread first. Propose closing as Works as designed, or turning this into a doc clarification.

    🔧cd609219f52023directory creation temporarily changes the umaskpatchREPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6) — and worse than "temporary": 8 threads running file mkdir in a loop leave the process umask permanently at 0000 (3/3…

    Open ticket cd609219f5 · 16. Commands A-H · filed 2023-04-05

    🔧 Since triage (updated 2026-10-25)

    Status now: Open

    • 🔧 2026-10-17 check-in 5d7e74108f on mkdir-no-umask-call, not merged: Fix cd609219f5 and 623585ffff: [file mkdir] read the umask with umask(0) + umask(mode), which threads could leave at 0 for the whole process, and masked the
    • 💬 2026-10-17 serhiy.storchaka: Confirmed, and worse than temporary: with several threads running [file mkdir], the process umask ends up permanently at 0, so later files are created world-writable (main, 9.0, 8.6). Proposed fix in branch mkdir-no-umask-call, with 623585ffff: call mkdir(path, 0777) and let the kernel apply the umask; umask() is not called any more. The permissions of new directories do not change. Test unixFCmd-5.2. The old co…
    Full verdict

    REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6) — and worse than "temporary": 8 threads running file mkdir in a loop leave the process umask permanently at 0000 (3/3 runs on main, 9.0 and 8.6; /proc/self/status shows the umask 0 thousands of times while the threads run). Also, with umask 0777, file mkdir makes a mode 000 directory, although the docs promise that u+rwx is always added.

    • Platform unix
    • Tested main (own build), 9.0 and 8.6 tip tcltest (testthread), Linux
    • Cause unix/tclUnixFCmd.c:DoCreateDirectory reads the umask with umask(0); umask(mode), which is process-wide and races between threads. It then passes (0777 & ~umask) | u+rwx to mkdir(), which applies the umask again and so drops the u+rwx it was meant to force.
    • Prototype prototypes/cd609219f5.patch (58 changed lines, ~20 in C; tests unixFCmd-5.2, unixFCmd-5.3) — mkdir(path, 0777) lets the kernel apply the umask, and then a chmod adds u+rwx only if the umask removed any of these bits. The umask is never touched. 5.3 (threads, then check that a new file is 0644 under umask 022) fails without the fix (666) and 5.2 fails too (umask 0777 → 0); unixFCmd.test (5×) and fCmd.test pass.
    • Suggested ticket comment Confirmed: with several threads running file mkdir, the process umask ends up permanently at 0 (main, 9.0, 8.6). Proposed fix: let mkdir() apply the umask and add u+rwx with chmod() afterwards, never calling umask(); tests unixFCmd-5.2/5.3.

    REPRODUCED (core.tcl-lang.org/tcl report rn=7, from the local clone's reportfmt)

    • Platform other (Fossil ticket report configuration, not Tcl code)

    • Cause WHERE ($login <> '' || status <> 'Deleted') uses ||, which is string concatenation in SQL, not OR, and binds tighter than <>.     • Prototype none (repository setting, needs an admin to edit report 7). Fix: WHERE (coalesce($login,'') <> '' OR status <> 'Deleted'), or just WHERE status <> 'Deleted' as in Tk.
    • Suggested ticket comment The report's WHERE clause uses || (string concatenation in SQL) instead of OR, so it is NULL for anonymous users and lists nothing. A ticket admin needs to change it to WHERE status <> 'Deleted' (as in Tk) or (coalesce($login,'') <> '' OR status <> 'Deleted').

    • Cause generic/tclCmdIL.c:Tcl_LsearchObjCmd — -bisect sets mode=SORTED plus bisect=1, and a later -exact resets mode to EXACT (a linear search), so the bisect flag is silently ignored. Per lsearch.n -bisect implies -sorted, and -sorted compares exactly anyway, so -exact should not cancel it.

Branch system-encoding-keep-retired is a simple alternative to sebres-encoding-perf-branch: former system encodings are kept until finalization, so a conversion can keep using the one it r…
    Full verdict

    REPRODUCED (main, 9.0) — crash; 8.6 has the same code (not run: no Thread 2.8 build)

    • Platform generic (threads)
    • Tested Thread 3.0.7 built in work-a1. Script: one thread loops file exists <600 KB path> (Tcl_UtfToExternalDStringEx with NULL encoding), main thread loops encoding system over koi8-r/koi8-u/cp1251/cp1252/iso8859-5/macCyrillic for 4 s. SEGV in 40/40 runs on 9.0.5, 10/10 on unpatched main, 3/3 under ASan (TableFromUtfProc via Tcl_UtfToExternalDStringEx/CheckAccess). With the prototype: 40/40 clean, 5/5 clean under ASan.
    • Cause generic/tclEncoding.c: the conversion functions use systemEncoding without taking a reference when encoding is NULL, so Tcl_SetSystemEncoding in another thread can free it mid-conversion. Second bug found on the way: Tcl_GetEncoding(NULL, NULL) increments the refCount of the system encoding under the mutex but then returns systemEncoding re-read *after* unlocking, so it can return a different, unreferenced encoding (same in 9.0 and 8.6).
    • Prototype prototypes/f2ff05fc84.patch (204 lines with context, 74 +/- lines, test thread-9.1, constraint thread): Tcl_GetEncoding returns the pointer it referenced; Tcl_ExternalToUtfDStringEx, Tcl_UtfToExternalDStringEx, Tcl_ExternalToUtfEx, Tcl_UtfToExternalEx and Tcl_ExternalToUtf take a reference with Tcl_GetEncoding(NULL, NULL) and re-enter themselves when encoding is NULL. That is one mutex lock/unlock pair per NULL-encoding conversion (the cost sebres objected to); encoding/io/chan/fCmd/cmdAH/utf tests pass, thread.test passes. Tcl_GetEncodingName(NULL) / Tcl_GetEncodingNulLength(NULL) still unprotected (the API cannot be fixed). sebres-encoding-perf-branch (8.5-based) is not merged.
    • Suggested ticket comment Reproduced on 9.0.5 and main: one thread doing file exists on a long path while another loops encoding system crashes every run. Also Tcl_GetEncoding(NULL, NULL) returns systemEncoding re-read after unlocking the mutex. Proposed fix: take a reference to the system encoding for NULL-encoding conversions and return the referenced pointer, test thread-9.1.

    • Tested test extension calling setenv() in Init, on main build (9.1.1), 9.0.5, 8.6.18. unset env(MYVAR) fails with "no such element in array"; unset -nocomplain env(MYVAR) silently leaves the variable in the environment (a later info exists env(MYVAR) is 1).
    • Cause generic/tclVar.c:TclObjUnsetVar2 (and the INST_UNSET_ARRAY* bytecodes) look up the element with createPart2=0, so for an element that exists only in environ the lookup fails before any trace runs and EnvTraceProc never calls TclUnsetEnv. Read traces (info exists, $env(X)) and array traces (array unset, array names) do resync, which is why array unset env MYVAR works.
    • Prototype none (needs a decision on generic trace semantics: e.g. fire read/array traces on a missing element before unset, or have the env array resync itself on unset; not env-local in the current design)
    • Suggested ticket comment Still present in 9.1/9.0/8.6: unset looks up env(X) without creating it, so no trace fires and TclUnsetEnv() is never called for a variable set behind Tcl's back. Workaround: info exists env(X) (or array unset env X) before unset.

    • Before thread-bug-3d768414de (child interp writes a buffered x to a file, then thread::send -async $t {set x 1} ::done resp. -command, vwait, interp delete; file size shows whether the interp was really deleted and its channel flushed) with threadCmd.c unpatched -> 0 0

    REPRODUCED (main + Thread 3.0.7, 9.0.5 + Thread 3.0.7, 8.6.18 + Thread 2.8.13)

    • Platform generic (Thread package)
    • Tested child interp with assoc-data delProc (work-a6/assoc) and with a buffered file channel. Plain package require Thread, thread::create/send/release, tsv, mutex, transfer and tpool all let the interp be deleted. thread::send -async $t script ::var and thread::send -command $t script cmd leave it alive: the delProc never runs and the channel is never flushed.

    • Suggested ticket comment Reproduced with Thread 2.8.13 and 3.0.7: thread::send -async with a result variable (or -command) Tcl_Preserve()s the caller's interp, and the routed-back callback never releases it, so the interp is never deleted. Proposed fix: release it in ThreadEventProc after running ThreadClbkSetVar/ThreadClbkCommand; test thread-bug-3d768414de. (Belongs to the Thread package.)

        Open ticket 934e6eb9cf · 21. [namespace] · filed 2020-01-03

        🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

        934e6eb9cf.patch: VERIFIED

        • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71)
        • Before work-a3/v934.tcl (the ticket script, plus a call from a proc and from a coroutine) -> unknown subcommand "x": namespace ::ns1 does not export any commands in all three cases
        • Patch applied cleanly (15 changed lines)
        • After one two three; from a proc caller continued: a b (the handler's tailcall does not replace the calling proc); in a coroutine it works too. Tests namespace (313/0 failed), tailcall, nre, oo, coroutine, apply: 0 failed
        • Test existing namespace-53.12 (from the patch) fails on the unpatched tip / passes after
        Full verdict

        REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.6.0)

        • Platform generic
        • Tested reporter's script on main build, 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.6.0: "unknown subcommand "x": namespace ::ns1 does not export any commands".
        • Cause generic/tclEnsemble.c:EnsembleUnknownCallback calls TclSkipTailcall() before a synchronous Tcl_EvalObjv() of the handler. That marks an NRCommand below the eval's callback root, so the handler's tailcall is deferred until after the whole ensemble command; the handler's result is empty, which means "reparse", and the reparse fails.
        • Prototype prototypes/934e6eb9cf.patch (15 changed lines, test namespace-53.12). Removes the TclSkipTailcall() call, so Tcl_EvalObjv pushes its own NRCommand and the tailcall runs inside the handler eval (deferredCallbacks is consumed by the ensemble command itself, so no outer mark leaks in). namespace, tailcall, nre, oo tests pass.
        • Suggested ticket comment Still present. EnsembleUnknownCallback() calls TclSkipTailcall() before a non-NRE Tcl_EvalObjv(), so the handler's tailcall runs only after the ensemble returns and the handler looks like it returned an empty list. Proposed fix: drop that call (test namespace-53.12).

        Open ticket f7afd3dbef · 60. NRE and coroutines · filed 2019-12-24

        🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

        f7afd3dbef.patch: VERIFIED (the side effect on other lookupNsPtr users, i.e. ensemble -map, oo forward and coroutine, noted in the triage, stays a behaviour change for a maintainer to accept)

        • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71)
        • Before reporter's script (tcltest f7af.tcl) -> namespace eval ns1 nosuchroutine -> hello, but apply {{} {tailcall nosuchroutine} ns1} -> invalid command name "nosuchroutine"
        • Patch applied cleanly (20 changed lines)
        • After both -> hello; tests tailcall.test 40 passed/4 skipped/0 failed, namespace.test 312/2/0, namespace-old.test 126/0/0, nre.test 29/0/0, basic.test 118/29/0, unknown.test 7/0/0, oo.test 373/16/0, ooNext2.test 57/5/0, coroutine.test 81/1/0, proc.test 37/1/0, apply.test 41/3/0, interp.test 384/7/0, safe.test 153/2/0
        • Test existing tailcall-bug-f7afd3dbef fails before / passes after
        Full verdict

        REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6)

        • Platform generic
        • Tested reporter's script on main build, 9.0.5, 8.6.18: apply {{} {tailcall nosuchroutine} ns1} gives "invalid command name" while the same call without tailcall uses ns1's handler.
        • Cause generic/tclBasic.c:TEOV_NotFound picks the unknown handler from varFramePtr->nsPtr. A tailcall runs in the caller's frame (global) with only iPtr->lookupNsPtr set to ns1 (TclNRTailcallEval), so ns1's handler is ignored.
        • Prototype prototypes/f7afd3dbef.patch (20 changed lines, test tailcall-bug-f7afd3dbef). TEOV_NotFound prefers lookupNsPtr's handler when lookupNsPtr is given and has one, then falls back as before. Side effect: the same applies to the other lookupNsPtr users (ensemble -map targets resolved in the ensemble's namespace, oo forwards in the object's namespace, coroutine creation) — arguably also right, but a behaviour change for those. tailcall, namespace(-old), nre, basic, interp, safe, oo, ooNext2, unknown, coroutine, proc, apply, execute, compile tests pass.
        • Suggested ticket comment Still present. TEOV_NotFound() chooses the handler from the current call frame's namespace, but a tailcall only sets the lookup namespace. Proposed fix: prefer the handler of the explicit lookup namespace (test tailcall-bug-f7afd3dbef); note that it also affects ensemble maps and oo forwards to missing commands.

        ⬜ab4307e01b2019changing [encoding system] can corrupt [encoding dirs]patchREPRODUCED (8.6); NOT-REPRODUCED on main, 9.0 and 8.7b1 (fixed as a side effect: zipfs initialisation sets the encoding search path through Tcl_Set…

        Open ticket ab4307e01b · 10. Objects · filed 2019-10-21

        🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

        ab4307e01b.patch: VERIFIED

        • Base core-8-6-branch (tip 326e1bf923); main is not affected (vab43.tcl gives same: 1 on the main tip)
        • Before work-a3/vab43.tcl (encoding system gb12345, read encoding dirs, switch back) on the 8.6 tip -> same: 0 now=#?home#?serhiy#?tcltk/tcl-triage#?wt#?a3#..., and later encoding convertto koi8-r -> unknown encoding "koi8-r"
        • Patch applied cleanly (34 changed lines). Checked the logic against TclSetProcessGlobalValue/TclGetProcessGlobalValue: pgv->value holds native bytes and the per-thread copy is decoded with the system encoding, so bumping the epoch alone is correct.
        • After same: 1 now=wt-a3-86/li..., koi8-r loads. Tests encoding, unixInit, cmdAH, env, fileName, main, basic: 0 failed
        • Test existing encoding-27.3 (from the patch) fails on the unpatched 8.6 tip / passes after
        Full verdict

        REPRODUCED (8.6); NOT-REPRODUCED on main, 9.0 and 8.7b1 (fixed as a side effect: zipfs initialisation sets the encoding search path through Tcl_SetEncodingSearchPath, which stores it with no encoding, so it is never re-converted)

        • Platform generic
        • Tested encoding system gb12345; encoding system utf-8; encoding dirs on main build, 9.0.5 (installed and the tip build with a filesystem TCL_LIBRARY), 8.7b1: unchanged. 8.6.18: garbage with embedded NULs (#?home#?serhiy#?tcltk/8.6/lib/tc^@...), and later encoding loads fail ("unknown encoding").
        • Cause generic/tclUtil.c:TclGetProcessGlobalValue. On a system encoding change it runs Tcl_UtfToExternal(old) and then Tcl_ExternalToUtf(new) on pgvPtr->value, which already holds native bytes, so the conversions go the wrong way. With a non-ASCII-compatible encoding such as gb12345 (double-byte only) this is lossy, and switching back cannot restore the value. The same code is still on main/9.0, but there it is only reached for PGVs whose initializer supplies an encoding (libraryPath, the initial encodingSearchPath without zipfs).
        • Prototype prototypes/ab4307e01b.patch, against core-8-6-branch (34 changed lines, test encoding-27.3, run in a subprocess so it sees the initial value). Keeps the native bytes and only starts a new epoch, so per-thread copies are decoded again with the new system encoding. While gb12345 is the system encoding the dirs read as gb12345 text, as native bytes should; after switching back they are exact again. The test fails without the fix; encoding, unixInit, cmdAH, env, fileName tests pass. The same change applies to main/9.0 as a latent fix.
        • Suggested ticket comment Reproducible in 8.6 only; in 8.7/9.x the search path is set via Tcl_SetEncodingSearchPath() at init and is not re-converted. Cause: TclGetProcessGlobalValue() converts the stored native bytes as if they were UTF-8. Proposed fix for 8.6: keep the native bytes and only bump the epoch (test encoding-27.3).

        • 🔧 2026-10-20 check-in 732583df8c on pkgs-shared-make-var, not merged: Fix 9cdb0d5858 and 8228750a0a: the bundled packages were always built as shared libraries, even with --disable-shared. Keep that default, so that [package r
        • 💬 2026-10-20 serhiy.storchaka: Same as 9cdb0d5858, where two proposed fixes are described: pkgs-respect-disable-shared and pkgs-shared-make-var.

        • Platform build
        • Tested read unix/Makefile.in configure-packages on main, 9.0, 8.6 (no build needed)
        • Cause unix/Makefile.in configure-packages passes $(PKG_CFG_ARGS) --libdir=... --enable-shared (8.6 also --enable-threads), so the forced --enable-shared always wins over anything in PKG_CFG_ARGS. PKG_CFG_ARGS is Tcl's own $ac_configure_args plus the PKG_CFG_ARGS environment variable (unix/configure.ac:39), so simply moving it last (as requested) would also make a Tcl configured with --disable-shared build static bundled packages, which package require from pkgs/ cannot load (pkgIndex.tcl uses load on a shared lib). 9.0 has the same in both the pkgs8 and pkgs loops.
        • Prototype none (needs a decision: e.g. append only the user's environment PKG_CFG_ARGS after --enable-shared, keeping Tcl's own args before it; or tell users to build the static package outside the Tcl tree)
        • Suggested ticket comment Still the same in main/9.0/8.6. --enable-shared is forced on purpose because bundled packages are loaded from shared libraries; a static itcl is better built separately with its own configure. If wanted, only the user-supplied PKG_CFG_ARGS environment value could be placed after --enable-shared.

        • Platform generic
        • Tested sebres' snippets on main build, 9.0.5, 8.6.18.
          • clock scan {10:00 GMT} -format {%H:%M %Z} -timezone :America/New_York -base 1556240400: 8.6 gives Apr 26 (date of base taken in the input zone), 9.0/main give Apr 25 like free scan (date of base taken in the -timezone zone). Format scan and free scan now agree (9.0 clock rewrite).
          • Free scan clock scan CET -base 100000000 -gmt 1 still keeps the base time of day in GMT and reads it as CET (99996400 = base − 1h) on all versions, while format scan gives midnight. This is the documented "no time given" difference between free and format scan, plus the open question which zone wins for the base parts. The fix proposed in the ticket (input zone wins) is not merged.
          • -timezone GMT+05 is POSIX TZ syntax (5 h west of UTC), so its opposite sign from +05 is correct, not a bug.
        • Cause library/clock.tcl / generic/tclClock.c take the missing fields from the base in the -timezone (or current) zone and apply the zone from the input only to the parsed fields.
        • Prototype none (precedence change, behaviour redesign)
        • Suggested ticket comment Since 9.0 format scan and free scan agree (date from base is taken in the -timezone zone). Whether a zone given in the input should win for the parts taken from -base is a design decision still open; GMT+05 vs +05 is POSIX TZ sign convention and works as documented.

        • Suggested ticket comment Still open on Windows for DLLs other than registry/dde (those are worked around by 364bd985d6). Unix is not affected because the temp copy is unlinked right after loading. Both proposals (MemoryModule, apn-bug-a8e4f76ce4) are unmerged and need a TIP.

The registry/dde workaround 364bd985d6 covers only Tcl's own packages, not a DLL loaded from an application zip.

        • Cause unix/tclUnixFCmd.c: DoRemoveDirectory adds u+rwx only to the directory passed to file delete; TraversalDelete does nothing for DOTREE_PRED, so read-only subdirectories keep their mode and unlink() inside them fails. file.n says -force "will attempt ... to change permissions".
        • Prototype prototypes/b43efdfd61.patch (27 changed lines, test fCmd-20.3). TraversalDelete adds u+wx on pre-order directories. It deliberately does not add u+r, so an unreadable subdirectory still fails (fCmd-20.1 unchanged, and the FTS and opendir code paths stay consistent, since the opendir path opens the directory before the pre-order callback). fCmd.test passes; fCmd-20.3 fails without the fix.
        • Suggested ticket comment Still in 9.1/9.0/8.6: only the top directory gets its permissions changed, subdirectories don't. Proposed fix: TraversalDelete makes each subdirectory owner-writable/searchable before deleting its contents (test fCmd-20.3).

Proposed fix with test oo-3.13. Constructors stay as they are, since an object mixin is normally added after construction.

          ⬜ca6a9e56592017Can't flush one line through a socket when using zlib compression/decompressionpatchREPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.6.6)

          Open ticket ca6a9e5659 · 57. zlib · filed 2017-09-29

          🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

          ca6a9e5659.patch: VERIFIED

          • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71)
          • Before zlib-17.1 (the reporter's case: server pushes deflate, puts a line, -flush sync; a separate tcltest process pushes inflate on a blocking localhost socket and does gets) with tclZlib.c unpatched -> timeout after 5 s
          • Patch applied cleanly (39 changed lines). I checked the loop on the tip: the new avail_in == 0 break is reached only after a decBytes > 0 round, so it never returns 0 (EOF) by mistake
          • After -> qwertyuiop (3/3 runs); tests zlib.test 73 passed/2 skipped/0 failed, http11.test 86/12/0, http.test 148/6/0
          • Test existing zlib-17.1 fails before / passes after
          Full verdict

          REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.6.6)

          • Platform generic
          • Tested reporter's server/client as two processes on 127.0.0.1 with main (30d8ccce48), 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.6.6. The client's gets returns only when the server closes (3 s later). A raw client shows the server does send the full sync-flushed block (18 bytes, ending 0000ffff), so the sending side is fine.
          • Cause generic/tclZlib.c:ZlibTransformInput, inflate side: after decompressing the bytes it got, it loops back to Tcl_ReadRaw on the parent whenever toRead is not yet satisfied. On a blocking channel that read blocks even though decompressed data is ready. Non-blocking channels break out on EAGAIN, so they are not affected.
          • Prototype prototypes/ca6a9e5659.patch (39 changed lines incl. 30 test lines, test zlib-17.1). Return what was decompressed once all buffered input is consumed (inStream.avail_in == 0) instead of reading more. zlib.test and http11.test pass; zlib-17.1 times out without the fix.
          • Suggested ticket comment Still in 9.1/9.0/8.6. The server sends the sync-flushed data; the inflate transform's input proc keeps reading the blocking socket instead of returning the bytes it already decompressed. Proposed fix: stop once buffered input is consumed (test zlib-17.1).

          ⬜77f0dbc0f82017Wrong errorstack when using slave interppatchREPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6)

          Open ticket 77f0dbc0f8 · 20. [interp] · filed 2017-07-26

          🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

          77f0dbc0f8.patch: VERIFIED

          • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71)
          • Before interp-31.2 FAILED: -errorstack INNER {returnImm {caught error} {}} UP 1 UP 1 (stale INNER from an earlier caught error)
          • Patch applied cleanly (test hunk offset 20 lines; 26 changed lines)
          • After interp-31.2 passes (INNER {invokeStk foo} ...); tests interp 385/0 failed, error 318/0, info 285/0, cmdMZ 96/0, execute 157/0, ioTrans 72/0, basic 118/0, proc 37/0, namespace 312/0, coroutine 81/0, nre 29/0, oo 373/0
          • Test existing interp-31.2 fails before / passes after
          Full verdict

          REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6)

          • Platform generic
          • Tested main (own build), 9.0 tip, 8.6 tip; stale INNER {returnImm {catched error} {}} from an already-caught error shows up in -errorstack after a child->parent alias error
          • Cause generic/tclResult.c:Tcl_GetReturnOptions puts iPtr->errorStack into the options even when iPtr->resetErrorStack is set (the stack is logically empty but still holds the previous error). The alias target in the parent fails without any Tcl_LogCommandInfo, so the reset never happens, and Tcl_TransferResult copies the stale list into the child; Tcl_SetReturnOptions then clears resetErrorStack in the child, so the child never adds its own INNER either.
          • Prototype prototypes/77f0dbc0f8.patch (26 changed lines, test interp-31.2). Tcl_GetReturnOptions reports an empty -errorstack when a reset is pending; Tcl_SetReturnOptions leaves the reset pending when it gets an empty -errorstack. Result is now INNER {invokeStk foo} CALL {run_in_slave foo}, which is what the reporter expected. interp, error, result, info, cmdMZ, execute, ioTrans, basic, proc, namespace, coroutine and nre tests all pass; full suite: only the pre-existing zipfs.test environment failures (they also fail on a clean build). Side effect: an explicit return -code error -errorstack {} now lets the next level record its INNER context.
          • Suggested ticket comment Tcl_GetReturnOptions() returned the stale error stack while a reset was pending, and Tcl_TransferResult() carried it into the child interp. Proposed fix with test interp-31.2 (prototype, not yet on a branch).

          ⬜46450b464e2017A namespace loses track of itselfREPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.5), but it follows from the documented semantics

          Open ticket 46450b464e · 21. [namespace] · filed 2017-06-02

          Full verdict

          REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.5), but it follows from the documented semantics

          • Platform generic
          • Tested main, 9.0 tip, 8.6 tip, 8.5.19: both reporter scripts behave as described on all of them
          • Cause after namespace delete [namespace current] the running namespace is NS_DYING. It stays current for the running code, but by design (namespace.n: "marked to prevent other code from looking it up by name") the name ::ns1 no longer resolves to it. namespace eval [namespace current] {} therefore creates a second ::ns1. Relative doc creates/looks up a child of the dying namespace, while apply ... ::ns1 runs in the new one. So two namespaces share the name ::ns1.
          • Prototype none (needs a design decision, e.g. refuse to create children in, or namespace eval into, a dying namespace, or have namespace current reflect the deleted state)
          • Suggested ticket comment Still the same on 8.5 through 9.1. Code that is still running in a deleted namespace keeps using it, but the name ::ns1 no longer finds it (as namespace.n documents), so namespace eval [namespace current] creates a new namespace under the same name. Changing this needs a design decision about what code running in a dying namespace may do.

          • Platform Windows
          • Verdict REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6) on the VirtualBox VM — backward steps of up to ~150 ms; whether native hardware shows it was not tested
          • Tested VM win/b7b707a310.tcl for 60 s each: clock microseconds went backwards 11 times on 9.1b1 (max 147005 us), 15 on 9.0.5 (max 117523 us), 12 on 8.6.18 (max 147041 us); on 9.1 microseconds vs monotonic drifted by up to 3.17 s. Control (work-win2/ck/ck.c, same 60 s): GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime never goes backwards (0 of 1.9e9 samples), but it drifts −1.3 .. +2.0 s against QueryPerformanceCounter, because the VM's virtual TSC and VBoxService time sync disagree. So on this VM the system clock itself is monotonic, and the backward steps come from Tcl's calibration.

The 2017 fix f6637d3dd8 (present in 8.6/9.0/main) limits but does not prevent this. Tcl never calls GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime (Win8+), which would make the whole calibration thread unnecessary.
          • Prototype none (owner sebres is working on the calibration; a switch to GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime would be a larger change)
          • Related on 9.0 the same clock disagreement triggers a ~72 min hang in Tcl_Sleep (separate bug, see the last section).

Maybe use GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime directly instead of the calibrated QPC?

TclInitCompileEnv sets atCmdStart = 1, and for codeNext == codeStart no INST_START_CMD is emitted and no count is recorded. Behaviour change: command limits now trip one command earlier, so interp-34.4..34.6 expected {6 4 b} changes to {5 5 b} and interp-34.7 4 to 5 (updated in the patch). Full suite: only the pre-existing zipfs.test environment failures remain (they also fail on a clean build).
          • Note compiled ensemble subcommands without their own compiler (e.g. info cmdcount) are counted twice, by INST_START_CMD and by Dispatch. This is pre-existing and not fixed.
          • Suggested ticket comment The first compiled command of each bytecode is never counted, because the compiler omits INST_START_CMD at offset 0. Proposed fix with test info-bug-931e4956b9 (prototype). It makes command limits trip one command earlier, so the interp-34.4..34.7 expectations change.

Proposed fix: copy argv for each call, test iortrans-bug-0ef291c1c2.

          Open ticket 57e44de76e · 07. Variables · filed 2015-07-05

          🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

          57e44de76e.patch: VERIFIED+TEST-ADDED (doc + behaviour-pinning tests)

          • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71); also applies to core-8-6-branch (offsets only)
          • Before trace.n says a trace on a whole array "is invoked whenever any element of the array is manipulated", and that a traced undefined variable is created without a value; nothing about element reads before it becomes an array. Behaviour (work-a1/57e4.tcl, identical on main and 8.6 tip): trace add variable a read tr; set a(x) -> can't read "a(x)": no such variable, trace not called (also compiled, from a proc); after array set a {} the same read calls the trace (read x) and returns the value it sets; a scalar read set b of a traced undefined variable does call the trace; trace add variable c(e) read tr makes c an array and its read trace fires.
          • Patch 59 changed lines. doc/trace.n (trace add variable): such a variable is not an array yet; reading an element fails with "no such variable" without invoking a read trace on name; whole-array traces fire for elements only once the variable is an array (after an element write or array set name {}); an element trace makes the variable an array. tests/trace.test: trace-41.1..41.3.
          • After man page renders, troff warnings 0/0. trace.test on main: 293 total, 289 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed.
          • Test added trace-41.1 (uncompiled read: error, no trace call, array exists 0; after array set tvar {} the trace fires and supplies the value), trace-41.2 (same through a compiled read in a proc, array made by an element write), trace-41.3 (element trace makes the variable an array and fires). Pins current behaviour: pass on main and on 8.6 tip (main's trace.test run with the 8.6 tcltest, -match trace-41.*: 3 passed).
          Full verdict

          REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.4)

          • Platform generic
          • Tested main build, 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.4.20; global and in a proc (compiled INST_LOAD_ARRAY): reading a(x) from a traced but undefined variable gives "no such variable" without firing the trace; after array set a {} the trace fires and can supply the value.
          • Cause tclVar.c Tcl_ObjGetVar2 (and the compiled load path) look up with createPart1=0, so TclLookupArrayElement returns NOSUCHVAR for an undefined non-array variable before any trace is called; a write uses createPart1=1 and turns it into an array, so later reads fire. trace.n only promises element traces for "a whole array", and an undefined traced variable is not yet an array.
          • Prototype none (calling read traces on an undefined non-array variable would change semantics on every read path, compiled and not; better a doc note)
          • Suggested ticket comment Still the same in 9.1/9.0/8.6. A read with createPart1=0 fails before traces run because the traced variable is not an array yet; array set a {} before adding the trace is the workaround. Suggest documenting this in trace.n rather than changing the lookup.

          ⬜50f67a3ace2014INST_START_CMD bug?REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6; for source not in 8.5)

          Open ticket 50f67a3ace · 47. Bytecode Compiler · filed 2014-11-27

          Full verdict

          REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6; for source not in 8.5)

          • Platform generic
          • Tested main build, 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.5.19 with set x [proc set args {puts FOO}]42: tclsh TT (direct eval) prints FOO and x stays unset everywhere; source TT sets x on 8.6+ (FOO and unset on 8.5); stdin (whole-command compile) sets x on all versions.
          • Cause the compiled set is inlined as INST_STORE_*; INST_START_CMD checks the compile epoch only before the command's words are substituted, so a redefinition from inside an argument is not seen until the next command. source is compiled since 42090a4d6 (NRE source in 8.6).
          • Prototype none (needs a second epoch check after word substitution for every inlined command, or the Tcl.n change dkf proposed: resolve the command after reading the first word; both are design decisions)
          • Suggested ticket comment Unchanged in 9.1/9.0/8.6: INST_START_CMD checks the epoch before the arguments are substituted, so an inlined command redefined from its own arguments still runs the old compiled version. Fixing it means another epoch check after the words, or defining that the command is resolved after its first word (dkf's proposal, a TIP).

          ⬜027ba061a82014Standard channels do not exist on new threads on WindowsREPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6)

          Open ticket 027ba061a8 · 69. Other · filed 2014-09-25

          Full verdict

          REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6)

          • Platform Windows (wish only)
          • Tested not on Linux — there threads get the real fd 0/1/2 so the issue cannot occur; code reading only.
          • Cause (by code): std channels are thread-specific (tclIO.c tsdPtr->stdinChannel…). In wish on Windows there are no std handles (GUI subsystem); Tk's console (tk/generic/tkConsole.c Tk_InitConsoleChannels → Tcl_SetStdChannel) installs console channels only in the thread that created the console, and TclpGetDefaultStdChannel finds no OS handles in a new thread. So this is really a Tk/console design point, as dgp noted in 2014.
          • Prototype none (needs a decision: e.g. Thread/Tk passing the console channels to new threads, or null channels)
          • Suggested ticket comment Cause: std channels are per-thread; in wish on Windows they are Tk console channels created only in the main thread, and a new thread has no OS std handles. Windows repro script prepared; probably belongs to Tk.
          Windows VM, run 2
          • Platform Windows (wish)
          • Verdict REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6)
          • Tested VM interactive session (scheduled task, wish started by wscript without std handles, main window withdrawn; script work-win2/027c.tcl) with Thread 3.0.7 / 2.8.13: the main thread has stderr/stdin/stdout (Tk console channels), a thread::create thread has none — puts stdout there fails with can not find channel named "stdout". Same on Tk/Tcl 9.1b1, 9.0.5, 8.6.18.
          • Cause std channels are per-thread (tclIO.c); Tk's console channels are installed only in the main thread, and a new thread finds no OS std handles in a GUI-subsystem process
          • Prototype none (design decision, probably for Tk/Thread)
          • Suggested ticket comment Confirmed with wish 8.6.18, 9.0.5 and 9.1 on Windows 11: threads created with thread::create have no stdout/stderr. The main thread's std channels are Tk console channels that exist only in that thread; a fix would need Tk (or Thread) to provide channels for new threads.

Proposed fix in branch normalize-dotdot-after-link, together with 3570244fff, 3183016fff and 3099612fff: on Unix the link target is normalized and further links are followed before backing up, s…
            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.5)

            • Platform generic (unix symlinks)
            • Tested main (own build), 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.5.19, 8.4.20 on Linux. With d/lx -> ../x: [file normalize d/lx/..] gives "<t>/d/.." (".." left in the result), d/lx/../.. gives "<t>/d" (should be the parent of <t>); with a trailing slash in the target (d/lx2 -> ../x/) d/lx2/.. gives "<t>/x" (should be <t>); the reporter's l -> ../f (a file) case gives t/d/f. Link chains (ll -> l -> ../x) back up to the wrong directory too.
            • Cause generic/tclPathObj.c:TclFSNormalizeAbsolutePath, ".." handling: the link target is pasted in literally (relative ones after the link's directory) and then the last element is cut off textually, so ".." / "." components or a trailing "/" in the target, or a target that is itself a link, give a wrong parent.
            • Prototype prototypes/3577801fff.patch (57 changed lines: 24 in tclPathObj.c, 33 tests filesystem-1.55, filesystem-1.56). Normalizes the substituted target with TclFSNormalizeToUniquePath, follows further links (max 32, so self-links terminate), strips trailing "/", then cuts the last element. All results now match realpath(1) / Python os.path.realpath; full test suite (minus http*) passes.
            • Suggested ticket comment Still present in 9.1/9.0/8.6: when ".." follows a symlink, the link target is used literally, so ".." or a trailing "/" in the target or link chains give a wrong result. Proposed fix: normalize the link target before backing up over it (patch with tests filesystem-1.55/1.56 available, not committed).

            ⬜3532972fff2012Tcl Scripts results in "called Tcl_FindHashEntry on deleted"REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6) only with TCL_FINALIZE_ON_EXIT=1; NOT-REPRODUCED with the default quick exit

            Open ticket 3532972fff · 80. Thread Package · filed 2012-06-07

            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6) only with TCL_FINALIZE_ON_EXIT=1; NOT-REPRODUCED with the default quick exit

            • Platform generic (Tcl finalization + Thread package)
            • Tested reporter's script with the delay cut to 300 ms (work-a6/t13.tcl), 40 runs per version and setting. Default: 0/40 failures on main, 9.0.5 and 8.6.18. TCL_FINALIZE_ON_EXIT=1: main 19/40, 9.0.5 37/40, 8.6.18 29/40, panicking with "called Tcl_FindHashEntry on deleted table" or "Tcl_Release couldn't find reference", or segfaulting.
            • Cause after thread::release, the worker is still tearing down its interp and its thread state (Tcl_FinalizeThread) while the main thread's exit runs a full Tcl_Finalize, which frees process-wide tables (preserve list, encodings, etc.) under it. Tcl_Finalize does not wait for other Tcl threads; this is the reason 8.6 made quick exit the default ([2001201]).
            • Prototype none (would need Tcl_Finalize to synchronize with or reap other Tcl threads, which is a design change; scripts can avoid it with -joinable + thread::join before exit: 0/40 failures on main and 8.6 with TCL_FINALIZE_ON_EXIT=1, work-a6/t13j.tcl)
            • Suggested ticket comment Still reproducible with TCL_FINALIZE_ON_EXIT=1 on 8.6/9.0/9.1: a full Tcl_Finalize races with a worker that was just released and is still finalizing. With the default quick exit it does not happen (0/40). Joining the worker before exit avoids it.

Building the list string rep for the trace callback's command argument is O(N). Branch bug-3485833 was never merged; the resolution "Fixed" refers only to the TclScanElement speedup.

            • 💬 2026-10-21 serhiy.storchaka: On main the timers are monotonic since TIP 723, but timed condition waits on Unix still used an absolute wall-clock deadline (default CLOCK_REALTIME condition variables, deadline from Tcl_GetDayTime()). A step of the system time during a timed wait made it longer or shorter by the size of the step. This affects every timed wait, including the 0-timeout one in zipfs init. Proposed fix in branch unix-monotonic-condw…
            • 💬 2026-10-21 oehhar: Would be great, if a Linux expert could verify. On MS-Win all is ok. Harald
            • 💬 2026-10-21 serhiy.storchaka: Harald, I tested it on Linux: with the wall clock shifted 1 hour forward by an LD_PRELOAD shim, after 2000 hangs with current trunk and takes 2 seconds with the branch. The full test suite passes on Linux, and the notifier, timer, thread and I/O tests on FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, DragonFly and OpenIndiana. Windows needs no change, since its waits use relative timeouts. macOS has no pthread_condattr_setclock(), so …
            • 💬 2026-10-21 oehhar: Thanks. Lets give other Linux folks one week of time. If there is no 2nd opinion, we will merge in one week. Thanks for all, Harald
            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (8.6; 9.0 by code reading in the select notifier and Tcl_ConditionWait); NOT-A-BUG on main (Tcl_SetTimeProc is unsupported since 9.1, TIP 723)

            • Platform unix
            • Tested small extension calling Tcl_SetTimeProc with time = real + 3600 s, then after 200 + vwait: 8.6.18 hangs (killed after 20 s), 9.0.5 on Linux works (epoll notifier, relative timeout). Main: Tcl_SetTimeProc panics "not supported in TCL 9.1"; notifier/timers use Tcl_GetDayTime/Tcl_GetMonotonicTime (TIP 723 merged in acb0a91c2c, 2026-01-08). Repro in work-a4/vt/.
            • Cause unix/tclUnixNotfy.c Tcl_WaitForEvent (8.6; 9.0: tclSelectNotfy.c, used where neither epoll nor kqueue exists) and unix/tclUnixThrd.c Tcl_ConditionWait add the timeout to the virtual Tcl_GetTime() to get an absolute time for pthread_cond_timedwait().
            • Prototype prototypes/3328635fff.patch (against core-8-6-branch; 16 changed lines, no test: there is no script-level access to Tcl_SetTimeProc). Uses gettimeofday() for the absolute deadline. Fixes the repro; timer.test, event.test pass. 9.0 needs the same change in tclSelectNotfy.c and tclUnixThrd.c.
            • Suggested ticket comment Still reproducible with 8.6 (and 9.0 with the select notifier): Tcl_WaitForEvent and Tcl_ConditionWait add the timeout to the virtual Tcl_GetTime() when computing the pthread_cond_timedwait() deadline. Proposed fix for 8.6/9.0: use the real time there. In 9.1 Tcl_SetTimeProc is no longer supported (TIP 723).

            ⬜3057639fff2010lappend inconsistency with respect to read tracesREPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.5) (the inconsistency msofer reopened with in 2012; the ::env part was fixed in 2010)

            Open ticket 3057639fff · 17. Commands I-L · filed 2010-09-01

            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.5) (the inconsistency msofer reopened with in 2012; the ::env part was fixed in 2010)

            • Platform generic
            • Tested main (own build), 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.5.19. With a read trace that sets the variable to 1, compiled lappend foo 2 gives 2 (no read trace) and eval lappend foo 2 gives 1 2 (trace fired). lappend ::env(NOSUCH) x works in both paths on all versions. appendComp-7.2..7.8 still carry the bug_3057639 constraint (never run).
            • Cause e6f97d1e4a (2010) dropped TCL_TRACE_READS from the INST_LAPPEND_* store flags (tclExecute.c, doStore*). Direct Tcl_LappendObjCmd (tclVar.c) still reads through TclPtrGetVarIdx: it fires read traces and silently ignores trace errors (treats them as "variable does not exist"), which is why the ::env/nonull case passes there. I tried adding TCL_TRACE_READS back to the 6 LAPPEND flag sites: compiled lappend then fires the trace (1 2), but appendComp-7.3/9.0/9.1 fail, because TclPtrSetVarIdx turns a trace error into a command error where the direct path ignores it. A consistent fix needs a decision: either "lappend fires read traces and ignores their errors" in both paths (new TclPtrSetVarIdx flag), or no read traces in either, like append. msofer and dgp considered this TIP-worthy.
            • Prototype none (needs a behaviour decision; experiment reverted)
            • Suggested ticket comment Still inconsistent on 8.6/9.0/main: compiled lappend skips read traces, direct lappend fires them but ignores their errors (the reason the ::env case works). Restoring TCL_TRACE_READS in INST_LAPPEND_* alone breaks appendComp-9.x, because TEBC would propagate trace errors. We need to decide which semantics we want (probably a TIP) before fixing.

            • 💬 2026-10-17 serhiy.storchaka: Still present in 8.6–9.1. Same cause as 3027822fff: the child's time-limit timer fires inside the limit handler's [vwait] and raises a background error in the busy child, whose bgerror handler cannot run because the limit is exceeded.             REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6; 8.5.19 shows the related #3027822 symptom instead)

            • Platform generic
            • Tested attached testInterpLimits2.tcl on main (9.1.1 build), 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.5.19 (40 s timeout). 9.x/8.6: "error in background error handler: time limit exceeded" each time the limit is renewed; 8.5: sin() returns {} ("Break now").
            • Cause same as #3027822: tclInterp.c TimeLimitCallback. The child exceeds its time limit at a command boundary, the limit handler (in the parent) runs [vwait], the child's still-pending time-limit timer fires inside it, Tcl_LimitCheck fails again (the active handler is skipped) and TimeLimitCallback calls Tcl_BackgroundException on the busy child. The child's bgerror handler cannot run because the limit is exceeded.
            • Prototype prototypes/3048170fff.patch (= 3027822fff.patch, 36 changed lines, test interp-34.15). TimeLimitCallback returns early if TCL_LIMIT_TIME is already marked exceeded (its handlers are running); a new limit re-arms the timer. Both attached scripts then run cleanly; interp/event/timer.test pass.
            • Suggested ticket comment Still present in 8.6–9.1. The child's time-limit timer fires inside the limit handler's &#91;vwait&#93; and raises a background error in the busy child. Proposed fix (shared with &#91;3027822&#93;): skip TimeLimitCallback while the time-limit handlers are running; test interp-34.15.

            🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

            3048057fff.patch: VERIFIED

            • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71)
            • Before out-of-tree TSan build of the tip (work-a2/v2/tsan, -fsanitize=thread -g -O1 -DPURIFY), 4 threads locking one static Tcl_Mutex (work-a2/v2/mtx.c, copied from work-a6): runmtx.sh 40 -> data race in 40/40 runs, at tclUnixThrd.c:647/662 (unlocked *mutexPtr read vs. store under globalLock in Tcl_MutexLock) and :109/:114 (PMutexLock owner field)
            • Patch applied with offset +8 (re-saved, 52 changed lines, content unchanged)
            • After same, 40 runs -> 0 runs with a race report; tests event, io, thread, notify, async, timer: 1176 total, 1090 passed, 86 skipped, 0 failed; with Thread 3.0.7 (TCLLIBPATH=work-a2/thread) thread, async, ioTrans, socket: 364 total, 360 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed
            • Test none possible in tcltest (needs a TSan build); the TSan program above is the repro
            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6 by code; ThreadSanitizer report on main)

            • Platform unix (generic double-checked locking; win/tclWinThrd.c has the same pattern)
            • Tested TSan build of main (work-a6/tsan, -fsanitize=thread -DPURIFY) with a 4-thread C program locking one static Tcl_Mutex (work-a6/3048057-mtx.c): data race reported 5/5 runs at tclUnixThrd.c:639 (unlocked *mutexPtr == NULL read) vs :648 (store under globalLock), exactly the ticket's report; plus a second race on the reentrant-mutex owner field (PMutexLock reads pmutexPtr->thread unlocked; 9.0/main only, 8.6 has no PMutex). With the prototype: 0 reports in 40/40 runs. 8.6 and 9.0 have the same unlocked read in Tcl_MutexLock/Tcl_ConditionWait.
            • Cause unix/tclUnixThrd.c Tcl_MutexLock/Tcl_ConditionWait/Tcl_ConditionNotify use double-checked locking with plain loads/stores of the lazily created pointer (no acquire/release), and PMutexLock/Unlock/PCond*Wait access the owner thread field without atomics. Benign on x86 in practice, formally a data race (could matter on weakly ordered CPUs).
            • Prototype prototypes/3048057fff.patch (52 changed lines incl. comment; no tcltest test, needs TSan; thread.test with Thread, event/socket/io.test and Thread's own suite pass) — GCC/clang __atomic acquire/release for the published pointers, relaxed atomics for the owner field; plain accesses on other compilers.
            • Suggested ticket comment Still present: ThreadSanitizer reports the unlocked *mutexPtr read in Tcl_MutexLock on 9.1 (and a similar one on the reentrant owner field in PMutexLock). Proposed fix: use __atomic acquire/release loads/stores for the lazily created mutex/condition pointers and relaxed atomics for the owner field (patch available, unix only).

            • Tested main, 8.6.18: in namespace eval ns, interp alias {} myputs {} puts creates ::myputs, interp alias {} ns::myputs2 {} puts creates ::ns::ns::myputs2 (and interp aliases lists the token ns::myputs2, not the real name).
            • Cause tclInterp.c TclAliasCreate passes the name to Tcl_CreateObjCommand2/Tcl_NRCreateCommand2, whose documented rule (CrtObjCmd.3) is: unqualified → global namespace, qualified → relative to the current namespace. [proc] resolves both relative to the current namespace.

            3046359fff.patch: VERIFIED+TEST-ADDED (after rework; the original prototype leaked the clientData)

            • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71)
            • Before new test command testnewnativepath /foo/bar (tclTest.c: a minimal registered "nativepath" filesystem whose internalToNormalizedProc caches its own native rep "cached:<path>" through Tcl_FSGetInternalRep; the command passes clientData "native:<path>" to Tcl_FSNewNativePath and reports the native rep kept and how many reps were freed after release) -> native:/foo/bar 2: the driver's cached rep is thrown away, as the ticket says
            • Patch applied cleanly (offset 6), but the ORIGINAL patch is BROKEN in one respect: it returns early for any path-typed object and never stores or frees clientData, so the clientData passed in leaks; the same test with the original patch gives cached:/foo/bar 1 (only one of the two reps freed). It also skipped the conversion when the intrep belonged to another filesystem (e.g. a driver that normalized through the native fs), so the new object was no longer tied to fromFilesystem. Reworked: return early only when the intrep's fsPtr is fromFilesystem; then store clientData if the native rep is still NULL, free it with freeInternalRepProc if the native rep is a different one. Otherwise the old code path. 17 changed lines in tclPathObj.c; with the new test filesystem and command in tclTest.c (~105 lines) and the test, 127 changed lines in all
            • After testnewnativepath /foo/bar -> cached:/foo/bar 2; tests fileSystem.test 142 passed/21 skipped/0 failed, cmdAH.test 16971/30/0, fCmd.test 260/45/0, fileName.test 259/47/0, unixFCmd.test 30/19/0, unixFile.test 7/0/0, zipfs.test (make test) 498/37/0

            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6; by code reading, unchanged)

            • Platform generic
            • Tested code reading of main/9.0/8.6 generic/tclPathObj.c. No core filesystem has an internalToNormalizedProc that sets a path intrep (zipfs has NULL), and nothing in the core calls Tcl_FSNewNativePath, so only extension filesystems are affected.
            • Cause generic/tclPathObj.c:Tcl_FSNewNativePath always frees the returned object's intrep and builds a new FsPath. If the driver kept clientData in its own FsPath, freeing that rep calls freeInternalRepProc on the same clientData that is then stored again (use-after-free), not just wasted work.
            • Prototype prototypes/3046359fff.patch (8 changed lines, no test: needs a test filesystem with internalToNormalizedProc); returns the object unchanged if it already has fsPathType. The fs/path tests pass (zipfs.test's 25 failures happen on an unpatched build too when TCL_LIBRARY is set).
            • Suggested ticket comment Still as described. Proposed fix: Tcl_FSNewNativePath returns the driver's object as is when it is already of the path type. That also avoids freeing clientData if the driver stored it in its own intrep.
