            Open ticket 3038316fff · 10. Objects · filed 2010-08-02

            🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

            3038316fff-86.patch: VERIFIED (doc only, no test possible)

            • Base core-8-6-branch (tip 326e1bf923). 8.6 only: since TIP 509 (8.7/9.0) Tcl mutexes are reentrant and the same-thread case no longer deadlocks (main survives the repro).
            • Before Encoding.3 says only "This freeProc function is called when the encoding is deleted"; no word about locking. Behaviour: work-a2/enc/encfree.c (copied to work-a1/enc; freeProc calls Tcl_GetEncoding/Tcl_FreeEncoding, then the last reference is dropped): timeout 5 wt-a1-86/unix/tcltest work-a1/encfree.tcl encfree86.so -> hangs, rc=124; main ... encfree91.so -> survived. Cause: tclEncoding.c FreeEncoding() calls freeProc with encodingMutex held (also from Tcl_SetSystemEncoding and TclFinalizeEncodingSubsystem); the functions taking that mutex in 8.6 are Tcl_GetEncoding, Tcl_FreeEncoding, Tcl_GetEncodingNames, Tcl_SetSystemEncoding, Tcl_CreateEncoding (and Init/Finalize).
            • Patch 10 changed lines, doc/Encoding.3 only: freeProc runs with Tcl's internal, non-reentrant encoding lock held; it must not call Tcl_GetEncoding, Tcl_GetEncodingFromObj, Tcl_FreeEncoding, Tcl_GetEncodingNames, Tcl_CreateEncoding, Tcl_SetSystemEncoding (directly or via e.g. Tcl_EvalObjEx), or wait for a thread that may call them.
            • After man page renders; troff warnings 1/1 (pre-existing).
            • Test none possible (a C-API locking note; a test would have to deadlock the test suite, and the documented rule is a restriction on callers, not behaviour Tcl can check).
            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (8.6 only; not on 8.7b1, 9.0, main)

            • Platform generic (deadlock seen on Unix 8.6)
            • Tested small extension (work-a2/enc/encfree.c) that creates an encoding whose freeProc calls Tcl_GetEncoding/Tcl_FreeEncoding, then drops the last reference: 8.6.18 hangs (timeout), 8.7b1, 9.0.5 and main print "survived".
            • Cause tclEncoding.c FreeEncoding calls freeProc with encodingMutex held (unchanged in all versions). Since TIP 509 (8.7/9.0) Tcl mutexes are reentrant, so a freeProc using encoding functions in the same thread no longer deadlocks; in 8.6 (pthread mutex) it does. A cross-thread lock-order deadlock is still possible in theory if the freeProc waits for a lock held by a thread that is calling encoding functions.
            • Prototype none (in 9.x the remaining risk is theoretical; for 8.6 a doc warning in Encoding.3 is the only cheap remedy, restructuring the locking is not small)
            • Suggested ticket comment Since TIP 509 (reentrant mutexes, 8.7/9.0) a freeProc may call encoding functions; in 8.6 this still deadlocks (freeProc runs with encodingMutex held). Suggest a one-line warning in Encoding.3 on core-8-6-branch and closing for 9.x.

            🔧2982713fff2010I cannot run exec command on Linux using Tcl/TkpatchREPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.4) when tclsh is started with SIGCHLD set to SIG_IGN by its parent

            Open ticket 2982713fff · 69. Other · filed 2010-04-06

            🔧 Since triage (updated 2026-10-25)

            Status now: Open

            • 🔧 2026-10-17 check-in b3c28a91a0 on tclsh-inherited-sigchld, not merged: Fix 2982713fff: if tclsh was started with SIGCHLD ignored (e.g. from system() in a program which ignores it), [exec] failed with "child process lost". Tcl_Mai
            • 💬 2026-10-17 serhiy.storchaka: Reproduced when tclsh is started with SIGCHLD ignored, as by system() from a program which ignores it, or env --ignore-signal=CHLD tclsh: the kernel reaps the children itself and waitpid() fails with ECHILD. Proposed fix in branch tclsh-inherited-sigchld: Tcl_MainEx() restores the default SIGCHLD handling if it is ignored. Applications which embed Tcl keep their own setting, as Tk now keeps the signal handlers of …
            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.4) when tclsh is started with SIGCHLD set to SIG_IGN by its parent

            • Platform unix
            • Tested env --ignore-signal=CHLD tclsh x.tcl and perl -e '$SIG{CHLD}="IGNORE"; exec @ARGV' tclsh x.tcl. exec echo yo fails with "child process lost (is SIGCHLD ignored or trapped?)", and exit codes are lost. Note: dash's trap '' CHLD (as in ferrieux's example) does not actually set SIG_IGN, but bash's does.
            • Cause with SIGCHLD set to SIG_IGN, the kernel reaps children itself and waitpid() in Tcl_WaitPid fails with ECHILD. Tcl already resets SIGCHLD to the default in its own children (RestoreSignals in unix/tclUnixPipe.c) and already sets SIGPIPE itself in TclpInitPlatform, but it never fixes an inherited SIG_IGN on SIGCHLD.
            • Prototype prototypes/2982713fff.patch (28 changed lines, test exec-23.1): TclpInitPlatform (unix/tclUnixInit.c) sets SIGCHLD back to SIG_DFL only if it is SIG_IGN at startup. Test exec-23.1 runs tclsh under bash -c "trap '' CHLD; exec ..." and checks that CHILDSTATUS ... 3 comes back. It fails without the C change. exec, process, pid, unixInit, event and io tests pass (1180 total, 0 failed). Trade-off: an embedding application that ignores SIGCHLD on purpose before initializing Tcl gets it reset. It can ignore it again afterwards, and [exec] cannot work in such a process anyway.
            • Suggested ticket comment Reproducible when the parent starts tclsh with SIGCHLD ignored (e.g. env --ignore-signal=CHLD tclsh): waitpid() then fails with ECHILD. Proposed fix: TclpInitPlatform resets an inherited SIG_IGN on SIGCHLD to SIG_DFL, as it already does for its children in RestoreSignals(). Test exec-23.1.

            • Suggested ticket comment (after the Windows run) On Windows OpenFileChannel reuses an existing channel with the same HANDLE, so a std handle closed behind Tcl's back is later matched with an unrelated CreateFile handle, and [open] returns stdin.

[source] then reads through that channel. No panic seen with this sequence.

            • Suggested ticket comment Still reproducible with 8.6, 9.0 and 9.1 by closing the std handle in the host: OpenFileChannel (win/tclWinChan.c) matches the recycled HANDLE value and &#91;open&#93; returns stdin.             • Platform unix
            • Tested reporter's nested >@stderr 2>@stdout script on main (own build), 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.4.20: prints ---- then OUT1/ERR1/OUT2/ERR2 (both inner streams to the middle stderr)
            • Cause unix/tclUnixPipe.c:TclpCreateProcess sets up the child's fds 0, 1, 2 in order (SetupStdFile in the fork path, posix_spawn_file_actions_adddup2 in the spawn path, which is what glibc >= 2.24 uses), so an errorFile that is fd 1 (or 0), or an outputFile that is fd 0, has already been overwritten by the time it is dup'ed. The parent now dups such fds to >= 3 (F_DUPFD, close-on-exec) before spawn/fork and closes the copies afterwards; covers both paths. (The 2009 dup-2.patch only patched the fork child.)
            • Prototype prototypes/2827015fff.patch (47 changed lines, test exec-15.8); exec.test, io.test, ioCmd.test, pid.test, process.test pass
            • Suggested ticket comment TclpCreateProcess sets up the child's stdin/stdout/stderr in sequence, so with 2>@stdout fd 1 has already been replaced by the exec pipe when stderr is dup'ed from it. Proposed fix: dup such fds above 2 in the parent first (fork and posix_spawn paths), test exec-15.8. Potential incompatibility: scripts that (mis)used 2>@stdout as 2>@1 will change behaviour.

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.5); regression since 8.5.0 (8.4.2-8.4.20 pass the original result to every trace)

            • Tested main (own build), 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.5.0, 8.5.1, 8.5.19 show second: first; 8.4.2, 8.4.11, 8.4.15, 8.4.20 show second: hello. leavestep traces behave the same (s2: s1).
            • Cause generic/tclTrace.c:TclCheckExecutionTraces and TclCheckInterpTraces save the interp state once, before the first trace, and restore it only after the last one. So trace N+1 gets trace N's result in its result argument. The final command result is still restored, which is why traced returns hello.
            • Prototype prototypes/2811381fff.patch (33 changed lines, test trace-40.2). After each successful trace, restore the saved state, so the next trace sees the command's own result (the 8.4 behaviour, and what trace.n says). trace, basic, proc, var, info and oo tests pass; trace-40.2 fails on 9.0 without the patch. The alternative is to document the chaining in trace.n, as the reporter asked.
            • Suggested ticket comment Since 8.5.0 each leave/leavestep trace gets the previous trace's result instead of the command's (8.4 passed the original). Proposed fix: restore the saved interp state after each trace (patch + test trace-40.2).
            ⬜2762041fff2009Fix (too) early recognition of EOF in a channel stackREPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6) for the generic problem; the original zlib/http symptom is gone (zbug.tcl gives 5000/5000 on all three, also with `zlib…

            Open ticket 2762041fff · 26. Channel Transforms · filed 2009-04-14

            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6) for the generic problem; the original zlib/http symptom is gone (zbug.tcl gives 5000/5000 on all three, also with zlib push ... -limit 4096)

            • Platform generic
            • Tested main (own build), 9.0.5, 8.6.18: attached zbug.tcl; plus work-a4/2762041-refchan.tcl — a [chan push] transform that buffers until EOF and returns 5000 bytes from drain: the first read $pr (read-to-EOF) returns only 4096 bytes, [eof] is already 1, and a second read returns the missing 904
            • Cause As Andreas analysed in 2010: CHANNEL_EOF lives in the shared ChannelState, so when the transform's Tcl_ReadRaw on the base channel hits EOF, generic/tclIO.c:DoReadChars (and GetInput callers) treats the whole stack as at EOF and stops, though the top transform still holds data (tclIORTrans.c keeps the rest of the drain result in its result buffer). The zlib channel avoids it by its read-ahead limit / own buffering, not by a generic fix.
            • Prototype none (needs a per-channel EOF flag or a "transform has pending data" check in the generic read loops; a design change beyond the size limit)
            • Suggested ticket comment The zlib/http symptom no longer reproduces, but the generic problem remains on 9.1/9.0/8.6: with a reflected transform whose drain returns more than one buffer, read-to-EOF returns early and [eof] is already true while 904 bytes are still in the transform; a second [read] returns them. Keep open as the reminder for a per-channel EOF.
            🔧2577420fff2009Tcl_GetInterpPath produces invalid path.patchREPRODUCED (main with ASan; 8.5 shows garbage paths; 8.6/9.0 have the same code, and the freed memory just still holds the old text). Heap use-afte…

            Status now: Open

            • 🔧 2026-10-17 check-in 49e00a9cd6 on interp-delete-callbacks-path, not merged: Fix 2577420fff: Tcl_GetInterpPath() and Tcl_GetParent() used freed memory in a Tcl_CallWhenDeleted() callback of a child interpreter. Unlink the child from it
            • 💬 2026-10-17 serhiy.storchaka: Still a use-after-free in 9.0 and 9.1 (ASan): the child's entry in the parent's child table is removed before the child's Tcl_CallWhenDeleted() callbacks run, and the InterpInfo may be freed before them too, because it is freed by another delete callback. 8.6 and 9.0 print the right path only because the freed memory still holds it. Proposed fix in branch interp-delete-callbacks-path: unlink after Tcl_DeleteInterp…
            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main with ASan; 8.5 shows garbage paths; 8.6/9.0 have the same code, and the freed memory just still holds the old text). Heap use-after-free.

            • Platform generic
            • Tested C extension work-a1/gip/gip.c (Tcl_CallWhenDeleted callback that calls Tcl_GetInterpPath(Tcl_GetParent(i), i)) with script work-a1/t10.tcl. 8.5.0, 8.5.6, 8.5.19 print garbage. 8.6.0, 8.6.18, 9.0.5 and main print the right paths, but main with ASan+PURIFY reports a heap-use-after-free in Tcl_GetInterpPath (freed hash entry). The rename child {} path also has a use-after-free in Tcl_GetParent (InterpInfo already freed).
            • Cause generic/tclInterp.c:ChildObjCmdDeleteProc deletes the child's entry in the parent's childTable before Tcl_DeleteInterp runs the child's delete callbacks. Also, InterpInfoDeleteProc is registered with Tcl_CallWhenDeleted, so depending on hash order it can free the InterpInfo before user callbacks run.
            • Prototype prototypes/2577420fff.patch (34 changed lines, no test: there is no script-level way to register a delete callback that calls Tcl_GetInterpPath; checked with the ASan repro). Delete the hash entry after Tcl_DeleteInterp. Replace the InterpInfoDeleteProc callback with TclInterpInfoDelete, which DeleteInterpProc calls after all assocData callbacks. ASan clean on all three deletion paths. Full suite passes (521526 tests, 0 failures, without http*/zipfs), and interp, safe and basic tests pass under ASan.
            • Suggested ticket comment Still a use-after-free on 9.1 (ASan): the child's childTable entry is removed, and the InterpInfo may be freed, before the child's Tcl_CallWhenDeleted callbacks run. Proposed fix: unlink after Tcl_DeleteInterp, and free InterpInfo after all delete callbacks.

            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6)

            • Tested main (own build), 9.0.5, 8.6.18: the ticket script still shows -leaky option in the error options; it also leaks into a later *successful* proc result (proc p {} {return -level 0 -leaky x; set y 1}; catch p m o gives o with -leaky).             • Prototype none (not a small change; needs a design decision in the bytecode engine, see also 2007198)
            • Suggested ticket comment Still reproducible in 9.1, 9.0 and 8.6, including leaks into a later successful result. Direct evaluation is fine; the bytecode engine never resets returnOpts between commands after a level-0 &#91;return&#93;.

            Open ticket 2345638fff · 49. Threading · filed 2008-11-25

            🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

            2345638fff.patch: VERIFIED+TEST-ADDED (only with --enable-symbols=mem / TCL_MEM_DEBUG or PURIFY builds; 8.6 has the same stub, not ported)

            • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71). Reproduced in an out-of-tree build work-a1/build-mem (wt-a1/unix/configure --enable-symbols=mem, so -DTCL_MEM_DEBUG=1 while the Makefile still has -DUSE_THREAD_ALLOC=1; tclInt.h #undef's USE_THREAD_ALLOC for TCL_MEM_DEBUG and PURIFY).
            • Before work-a1/build-mem/gmi (work-a6/tsan/gmi.c: Tcl_FindExecutable + Tcl_GetMemoryInfo) -> Tcl_GetMemoryInfo called when threaded memory allocator not in use, SIGILL (rc 132). Same through the new test command: build-mem/tcltest work-a1/gmi.tcl -> same panic, rc 132; build-mem/tcltest tests/thread.test -match thread-9.* (new tests, fix removed) -> panic, rc 132. The normal build returns the stats (2 caches: thread0x..., shared).
            • Patch 79 changed lines (fix 10 + doc 6; the rest is the test command). generic/tclThreadAlloc.c: the non-threaded-allocator Tcl_GetMemoryInfo stub appends nothing instead of panicking. Why empty: the result is documented as a list-of-lists with one list per allocator cache; without the threaded allocator there are no caches, so an empty list is exactly true, and callers that parse the list (AOLserver/NaviServer stats pages) keep working; a "note" element would break such parsers, and a panic kills a server for asking for statistics. doc/Alloc.3: one list per cache; without the threaded allocator (TCL_MEM_DEBUG, PURIFY) nothing is appended (also fixes the missing full stop in the old sentence). generic/tclTest.c: new testmemoryinfo command; it calls (Tcl_GetMemoryInfo)(&ds) directly, because tclTest.c is stub-enabled and the Tcl_GetMemoryInfo stub macro aborts with "Cannot call Tcl_GetMemoryInfo from stubbed extension" (the tcltest executable links libtcl, so the direct call resolves). tests/thread.test: constraints testmemoryinfo, memory; tests thread-9.1, 9.2.
            • After build-mem: gmi -> len=0, rc 0; tcltest gmi.tcl -> 0; thread-9.1 and 9.2 pass. Normal build: thread-9.1 passes, 9.2 skipped (memory); thread.test 57 total, 4 passed, 53 skipped (no Thread package), 0 failed. Alloc.3 troff warnings 0/0.
            • Test added thread-9.1 (testmemoryinfo returns a list whose elements are shared/thread... lists, including shared if non-empty; constraint testmemoryinfo) and thread-9.2 (empty result when the threaded allocator is not used; constraints testmemoryinfo memory). In the --enable-symbols=mem build both fail before (process panics) and pass after; in the normal build 9.1 passes before and after.
            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6; only with --enable-symbols=mem or -DPURIFY) — documented limitation rather than a bug

            • Platform generic
            • Tested C program calling Tcl_GetMemoryInfo: main PURIFY build panics "Tcl_GetMemoryInfo called when threaded memory allocator not in use"; normal main build returns the stats. Same stub in 8.6 tclThreadAlloc.c:1152 and 9.0.
            • Cause generic/tclInt.h #undef's USE_THREAD_ALLOC for TCL_MEM_DEBUG and PURIFY builds, so tclThreadAlloc.c compiles the panicking stub although tclConfig.sh still lists -DUSE_THREAD_ALLOC=1. doc/Alloc.3 already says it is only available with the threaded allocator; in 9.x a script can check tcl::build-info memdebug/purify (Tcl 9 is always threaded). A configure switch for the allocator does not exist (RFE part not done).
            • Prototype none (would be a behaviour decision: e.g. append nothing instead of panicking)
            • Suggested ticket comment Still as designed: with TCL_MEM_DEBUG or PURIFY the threaded allocator is disabled and Tcl_GetMemoryInfo panics (documented in Alloc.3). In 9.x the build can be checked with &#91;tcl::build-info memdebug&#93; / &#91;tcl::build-info purify&#93;. Making it a no-op instead of a panic would be a small change if wanted.

            Open ticket 1967630fff · 40. Dynamic Loading · filed 2008-05-20

            🔧 Since triage (updated 2026-10-25)

            Status now: Open

            • 🔧 2026-10-25 check-in 1773409c76 on unix-dlerror-mutex, not merged: Fix 1967630fff: tclLoadDl.c dlerror() is not thread safe. On NetBSD and OpenBSD the dlerror() state is process-wide, so a failing [load] in one thread could g
            • 💬 2026-10-25 serhiy.storchaka: Reproduced on NetBSD 10.1 and OpenBSD 7.9, where the dlerror() state is process-wide: a failing [load] concurrent with a successful [load] in another thread gets the other thread's message or NULL, and NULL crashes in Tcl_ObjPrintf(). Linux, FreeBSD and macOS keep it per thread. Proposed fix in branch unix-dlerror-mutex, based on the attached patch: a mutex from dlopen()/dlsym() until dlerror() has been read, and …
            🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

            1967630fff.patch: VERIFIED (fix proven with an emulating shim, 40 runs before/after; no test in the suite)

            • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71). Threaded build (wt-a1/unix), Thread 3.0.7 built in work-a1/thread/build-a1 against it. Hunks 3-5 do not apply to core-8-6-branch (different code around dlopen); same approach would port by hand.
            • Before on glibc dlerror() is thread-local, so the race cannot occur natively: dl/runmany.sh tclsh 40 400 "" -> SUMMARY runs=40 ok=40 wrong=0 crash=0. To reproduce the NetBSD/OpenBSD behaviour (process-global dlerror, confirmed there in result-unix-1.md) on Linux I wrote an LD_PRELOAD shim work-a1/dl/globaldlerror.c: dlopen()/dlsym() failures store the message in one global buffer, dlerror() returns and clears it, plus usleep(20) after each call. Note that [load] already serialises Tcl_LoadFile with tclLoad.c's libraryMutex, which is why plain failing-[load] stress (dl/dlerr.tcl, 3 threads) never showed anything even with the shim. But the Tcl_FindSymbol calls for *_SafeInit/*_Unload/*_SafeUnload after a successful load run outside that mutex. work-a1/dl/dlerr2.tcl: thread L loads 400 distinct copies of dltest/tcl9pkga.so (which lacks those symbols, so dlsym fails), threads AAAA/BBBB [load] missing files 1600 times each. With the shim: dl/runmany.sh tclsh 40 400 dl/globaldlerror.so -> SUMMARY runs=40 ok=0 wrong=0 crash=40: every run SEGFAULTs. gdb: AppendPrintfToObjVA <- Tcl_ObjPrintf("couldn't load file \"%s\": %s") <- TclpDlopen (tclLoadDl.c:132) <- Tcl_LoadObjCmd: the other thread's failing dlsym() + dlerror() consumed the message, so this thread's dlerror() returned NULL and TclpDlopen passed NULL to %s (FindSymbol already guards NULL with "unknown", TclpDlopen does not). So on NetBSD/OpenBSD a failed [load] concurrent with a successful [load] in another thread can crash Tcl, not just give a wrong message (not run on the VMs; the shim emulates their documented behaviour).
            • Patch 16 changed lines, unix/tclLoadDl.c only: Tcl-private TCL_DECLARE_MUTEX(dlMutex) held from the first dlopen() until the error message has been copied into the interp result (unlocked on the encoding-error early return and on both exits), and in FindSymbol from the first dlsym() until after dlerror()/the error message; plus the NULL guard ("unknown") for dlerror() in TclpDlopen, like FindSymbol has. Tcl mutexes are reentrant on main (TIP 509), so a library constructor that calls Tcl_LoadFile in the same thread does not deadlock. tclLoadDyld.c (macOS) not changed: Apple's dlerror() keeps per-thread state, so it is not affected. As noted in triage, the mutex only covers Tcl's own calls, not dlopen() by other code in the process.
            • After with the shim dl/runmany.sh tclsh 40 400 dl/globaldlerror.so -> SUMMARY runs=40 ok=40 wrong=0 crash=0 (each run: L 0, AAAA 0, BBBB 0 wrong); without the shim 40/40 ok. After fossil revert + rebuild the shim run crashes again (3/3). load.test 30/30 passed, unload.test 27/27 passed.
            • Test none added. Without the shim it never fails on Linux (40/40 before), and a suite test would need the Thread package, an LD_PRELOAD shim and hundreds of library copies, so it is neither cheap nor meaningful on the platforms where the suite usually runs. The reproducer is kept in work-a1/dl (globaldlerror.c, dlerr2.tcl, runmany.sh; copies/ is 47 MB and can be regenerated with a cp loop). On NetBSD 10.1 dlerr2.tcl without the shim should show the crash/wrong messages before the fix.

            1967630fff.patch (native NetBSD/OpenBSD): VERIFIED natively. The bug is real on NetBSD 10.1 and OpenBSD 7.9: in 40 runs, 33/40 (NetBSD) and 24/40 (OpenBSD) fail before the patch, half of them by SIGSEGV. With the patch, 0/40 fail on both.

            • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71, fossil tarball trunk), unpatched and with prototypes/1967630fff.patch (patch -p0), built natively on NetBSD 10.1 (gcc) and OpenBSD 7.9 (clang) in /tmp: unix/configure (threaded by default), gmake, gmake tcltest, unix/dltest built (tcl9pkga.so). Thread trunk (39d9f08aa0, 3.0.7) with tclconfig trunk in its tclconfig/, built against each Tcl build dir. 400 copies of the unpatched build's dltest/tcl9pkga.so made with a cp loop on each VM.
            • dlerror() is process-wide on both: work-a1/dl/dlerrt.c (a second thread makes dlopen() fail and is joined, then main calls dlerror()) prints the other thread's message on both: NetBSD Cannot open "/nonexist-B.so", OpenBSD File not found -> VERDICT: dlerror state is PROCESS-WIDE.
            • Repro work-a1/dl/dlerr2-bsd.tcl = dlerr2.tcl with one change. The glibc message pattern (...: /nonexist-X.so: *) does not fit the BSD loaders, and OpenBSD's message has no file name at all. So each failing load is now compared with the message the same [load] gives single-threaded before the threads start. Thread L loads pkga1..400.so; AAAA/BBBB each [load] a missing file 1600 times. Driver work-a1/dl/runvm-bsd.sh (ulimit -c 0, timeout 120 per run; reports ok/wrong/crash/hang). Each build ran 40 times with the same parameters (n=400).
            • Before (unpatched), reproduced natively on both, no shim:
              • NetBSD: SUMMARY runs=40 ok=7 wrong=13 crash=20 hang=0. All 20 crashes are rc=139 (SIGSEGV). Wrong messages are another thread's dlsym() error delivered as a failed [load] result, e.g. couldn't load file "/nonexist-AAAA.so": Undefined symbol "_Pkga_SafeUnload". Some are garbled, because the shared buffer was overwritten while being read: Undefined symbol "xist-ASafeUnl and Undefined symbol exist-AAAA.so".
              • OpenBSD: SUMMARY runs=40 ok=16 wrong=4 crash=20 hang=0. All 20 crashes are rc=139. Wrong messages: couldn't load file "/nonexist-AAAA.so": Unable to resolve symbol.
              • The crashes fit the NULL-to-%s path found with the Linux shim (TclpDlopen <- Tcl_ObjPrintf). I could not get a native backtrace: under gdb the race never fired (3+8 tries on OpenBSD, gdb 6.3; 3 tries on NetBSD), and one NetBSD gdb run hung (killed by PID). No core files (ulimit -c 0).
            • Patch unchanged prototypes/1967630fff.patch (16 changed lines, unix/tclLoadDl.c).
            • After (patched): NetBSD SUMMARY runs=40 ok=40 wrong=0 crash=0 hang=0; OpenBSD SUMMARY runs=40 ok=40 wrong=0 crash=0 hang=0. In the patched tree, gmake test TESTFLAGS="-file \"load.test unload.test\"" gives Total 57 Passed 57 Skipped 0 Failed 0 on both (load.test + unload.test).
            • Test none added, for the same reason as above: it needs the Thread package and hundreds of library copies. The repro is work-a1/dl/dlerr2-bsd.tcl + runvm-bsd.sh + dlerrt.c.
            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED at the libc level (NetBSD 10.1 often, OpenBSD 7.9 rarely); NOT-REPRODUCED through Tcl [load] (main, 4 threads, both OSes)

            • Platform unix
            • Tested code reading of unix/tclLoadDl.c on main: dlerror() is still called without a mutex after dlopen() (line ~129) and dlsym() (line ~226). The second half of the ticket (TclpFindSymbol reporting into interp) is already done: the error now goes into interp.
            • Cause unix/tclLoadDl.c:TclpDlopen/FindSymbol: dlerror() isn't required to be thread-safe by POSIX (before POSIX.1-2024).
            • Prototype none (a Tcl-private mutex would only protect Tcl's own load calls, not dlopen() done by extensions or libraries. Low practical value.)
            • Suggested ticket comment The interp-error half was done long ago. The remaining issue only matters on libcs with a global dlerror buffer (glibc, musl and FreeBSD use thread-local state). A Tcl-internal mutex would not cover dlopen() calls by other code. To check on the NetBSD/OpenBSD VMs whether it's still relevant there.
            Unix VMs, run 1
            • Platform unix (NetBSD, OpenBSD)
            • Verdict REPRODUCED at the libc level (NetBSD 10.1 often, OpenBSD 7.9 rarely); NOT-REPRODUCED through Tcl [load] (main, 4 threads, both OSes)
            • Tested C tests with two pthreads calling dlopen() on files that fail differently and checking dlerror() (work-unix1/scripts/dlerr.c; dlerr2.c for OpenBSD, whose messages have no file name, so it pairs a missing file with a non-ELF file). NetBSD 10.1: about 7–9% of 200000 calls per thread get NULL or the other thread's message (e.g. Cannot open "/nonexist-BBBB.so" in thread AAAA). OpenBSD 7.9: 1 NULL in 200000 (2 runs; ld.so serializes dlopen, so the window is tiny). Tcl tests (dlerr.tcl / dlerr2.tcl): 3–4 Thread-package threads load failing files 100000–300000 times each and check that the message matches their own failure. 0 wrong on NetBSD (3.6 million loads) and OpenBSD (3 runs × 400000).
            • Cause unix/tclLoadDl.c:TclpDlopen/FindSymbol read dlerror() right after dlopen()/dlsym() without a lock. On NetBSD and OpenBSD the error buffer is process-global, and dlerror() clears it.
            • Prototype none (a Tcl-private mutex around dlopen()+dlerror() and dlsym()+dlerror() would be about 15 lines, but it would not cover dlopen() calls from other code, and Tcl never hit the race in these runs, so a fix could not be verified)
            • Suggested ticket comment Confirmed at the C level: dlerror() is process-global on NetBSD 10.1 (concurrent dlopen() failures often get the other thread's message or NULL) and on OpenBSD 7.9 (very rare). Through &#91;load&#93; with 4 threads it never showed up. A mutex in tclLoadDl.c would only cover Tcl's own calls. Low priority.

            • Suggested ticket comment Still reproducible with Tk 9.1b1 and 8.6.18: "+1 display lines" in a -wrap word text returns an index in the middle of the UTF-8 sequence of "ä", so [.t get] returns the lone lead byte (U+00C3) and a strict [puts] fails.             • Suggested ticket comment The -nocase uses were replaced by TclUtfCasecmp long ago, but strcasecmp/strncasecmp are still used (clock, serial channel options) without <strings.h>, so strict POSIX compiles (or dietlibc) fail.             ⬜1157137fff2005Cannot open file if parent directory unreadable on SolarisREPRODUCED (main, 8.6 on OpenIndiana)

            Open ticket 1157137fff · 37. File System · filed 2005-03-05

            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 8.6 on OpenIndiana)

            • Platform unix (Solaris)
            • Tested Linux main/8.6 with a real chmod 111 parent: works (Linux getcwd() is a syscall). With getcwd() failing: [open file] and [glob *] fail with "error getting working directory name", and [file exists file] silently returns 0.
            • Cause generic/tclIOUtil.c:Tcl_FSGetCwd re-checks the native cwd on every relative-path normalization and, when getcwd() fails, deliberately resets the cached cwd and errors (pwd error is tested). Relative opens therefore depend on getcwd().
            • Prototype none (needs a design decision: fall back to the cached cwd for normalization while keeping [pwd]'s error)
            • Suggested ticket comment Still in the code: any relative path needs Tcl_FSGetCwd(), which fails if getcwd() fails, as it does on old Solaris with an unreadable parent. Modern Linux is not affected; someone with Solaris/illumos should check whether getcwd() still fails there.
            • To run on OpenIndiana mkdir -p /tmp/d1/d2; echo J > /tmp/d1/d2/file; chmod 111 /tmp/d1; cd /tmp/d1/d2; echo 'puts [gets [open file]]' | tclsh
            Unix VMs, run 1
            • Platform unix (Solaris/illumos)
            • Verdict REPRODUCED (main, 8.6 on OpenIndiana)
            • Tested OpenIndiana, as a normal user: mkdir -p /tmp/d1/d2; echo J >/tmp/d1/d2/file; chmod 111 /tmp/d1; cd /tmp/d1/d2. /usr/bin/pwd fails ("cannot determine current directory: Permission denied"). Both main and 8.6: pwd errors with "error getting working directory name: permission denied", open file fails with the same error, file exists file returns 0, and glob * gives "couldn't determine the current working directory". Opening by absolute path works.
            • Cause generic/tclIOUtil.c:Tcl_FSGetCwd: illumos getcwd() still needs read access to every ancestor, and Tcl resolves every relative path through the cwd. When getcwd() fails, relative paths fail (and [file exists] wrongly says 0).
            • Prototype none (needs a design decision: e.g. pass relative native paths through unchanged, or fall back to "." when getcwd() fails, while [pwd] keeps its error)
            • Suggested ticket comment Still happens on OpenIndiana with main and 8.6: in a directory with an unreadable parent, &#91;open file&#93; and &#91;glob *&#93; fail with "error getting working directory name: permission denied", and &#91;file exists file&#93; returns 0, because every relative path goes through getcwd(). Fixing this needs a fallback for relative paths when the cwd is unknown.

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.5, 8.4): the cached [file normalize] result goes stale. Since 8.5 [open] no longer reads the wrong file (8.4.20 did); only the normalized value is wrong.

            Open ticket 886457ffff · 26. Channel Transforms · filed 2004-01-28

            🧪 Prototype check (2026-10-24)

            886457ffff.patch: VERIFIED (behaviour change for C transforms stacked with a narrower mask: needs core review, as triage said)

            • Base main (tip d6dd6d0f71)
            • Before work-a4/v4trans.tcl: read-only reflected transform pushed on an r+ file: puts $f xyz; flush $f -> write not supported by Tcl driver; write-only transform: gets -> read not supported by Tcl driver (the channel stays R/W)
            • Patch applied cleanly (38 changed lines). Rebuilt all objects including tclIO.h (tclIO/IOCmd/IOGT/IORChan/IORTrans/IOUtil/CmdAH/Zlib/UnixChan/Test).
            • After -> channel "file5" wasn't opened for writing / ... wasn't opened for reading; after chan pop writing works again; make test TESTFLAGS="-file 'io.test ioCmd.test iogt.test ioTrans.test chan.test chanio.test zlib.test socket.test ioUtil.test'" -> 2473 total, 2284 passed, 189 skipped, 0 failed
            • Test existing iortrans-bug-886457 fails before (Result was 0 {} 0 {}: the buffered puts does not even report an error) / passes after
            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6)

            • Platform generic
            • Tested chan push of a read-only reflected transform (methods initialize/finalize/read) on an r+ file: puts goes to the transform driver and fails with "write not supported by Tcl driver" instead of the generic "channel wasn't opened for writing"; the same for a write-only transform and gets. The same on main, 9.0, 8.6. ChnlStack.3 says "a read-write channel may become read-only after the Tcl_StackChannel call", but Tcl_StackChannel only checks that the mask overlaps.
            • Cause generic/tclIO.c:Tcl_StackChannel never applies mask to statePtr->flags; Tcl_UnstackChannel resets the flags to maxPerms.
            • Prototype prototypes/886457ffff.patch (38 changed lines: new Channel.permMask field in tclIO.h; Tcl_StackChannel clears the R/W flags the new layer doesn't allow; Tcl_UnstackChannel restores the flags allowed by the remaining layer after the close; test iortrans-bug-886457). The test fails without the fix. With it: io, ioCmd, iogt, ioTrans, chan, chanio, zlib and socket tests all pass, and the full suite has only the usual 25 zipfs failures (TCL_LIBRARY run). A visible behaviour change for C transforms registered with a narrower mask than the channel, so it needs core review.
            • Suggested ticket comment Still true: Tcl_StackChannel only checks that the mask overlaps the channel mode and never restricts the channel, so writes reach a read-only transform's driver. Proposed fix: record the mask per layer, clear the disallowed flags on stack and restore them on unstack (test iortrans-bug-886457).

            ⬜696707ffff2003trace command on 'env' bugREPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.4) — but it follows from documented trace semantics (traces on a variable are disabled while one of its traces runs)

            Open ticket 696707ffff · 08. Environment Variables · filed 2003-03-03

            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.4) — but it follows from documented trace semantics (traces on a variable are disabled while one of its traces runs)

            • Platform generic
            • Tested reporter script on main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.4
            • Cause traces fire newest first, so the user's read trace runs before Tcl's own EnvTraceProc; its [set ::env($e) ...] does not fire EnvTraceProc's write trace (traces are inactive during a trace), so setenv() is never called, and then EnvTraceProc's read branch finds no such variable in the environment and fails the read. Afterwards env(TEST2) holds a value that is not in the real environment ([info exists] 1). With the 845241 prototype the stale value is cleared instead ([info exists] 0), which is more consistent but still fails the read
            • Prototype none (would need trace-order or nested-trace changes; a "keep the Tcl-side value" rule in EnvTraceProc conflicts with the 845241 fix)
            • Suggested ticket comment Still the case: the user's read trace runs before Tcl's env trace, and a write made inside a trace does not fire the env write trace, so the variable never reaches the environment and the env read trace reports it missing. This follows from the documented rule that traces are disabled while a trace runs; suggest documenting it in tclvars.n (env) rather than changing the trace machinery.

            🔧623585ffff2002[file mkdir] does not use default aclpatchREPRODUCED (main, 8.6; same code in 9.0)

            Open ticket 623585ffff · 37. File System · filed 2002-10-15

            Status now: Open

            • 🔧 2026-10-17 check-in 5d7e74108f on mkdir-no-umask-call, not merged: Fix cd609219f5 and 623585ffff: [file mkdir] read the umask with umask(0) + umask(mode), which threads could leave at 0 for the whole process, and masked the
            • 💬 2026-10-17 serhiy.storchaka: Still present on Linux: DoCreateDirectory() applies the umask to the mode itself, and when the parent has a default ACL (so the kernel does not apply the umask) this mode cuts down the inherited permissions. Proposed fix in branch mkdir-no-umask-call, with cd609219f5: call mkdir(path, 0777) and let the kernel apply the umask or ACL, as mkdir(1) does. Test unixFCmd-21.1.
            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 8.6; same code in 9.0)

            • Platform unix
            • Tested main (own build), 8.6.18 on Linux ext4 with setfacl -d u::rwx,g::rwx,o::rwx and umask 022. mkdir(1) gives group::rwx other::rwx, [file mkdir] gives r-x/r-x.
            • Cause unix/tclUnixFCmd.c:DoCreateDirectory masks the umask into the mode passed to mkdir(). When the parent has a default ACL the kernel ignores the umask, and the mode argument then cuts down the inherited ACL. The masking is redundant otherwise (mkdir applies the umask anyway, and the "force owner rwx" part never worked: umask 0700 still gives 0077). The umask(0)/umask(old) pair is also racy in threaded programs.
            • Prototype prototypes/623585ffff.patch (24 changed lines, test unixFCmd-21.1, constraint defaultAcl = setfacl works). Calls mkdir(path, 0777) and lets the kernel apply umask/ACL. Results for umask 077/022/0700 are unchanged; unixFCmd/fCmd/fileSystem/cmdAH pass.
            • Suggested ticket comment Still present on Linux: DoCreateDirectory() pre-applies the umask, which overrides the parent's default ACL. Proposed fix: call mkdir(path, 0777) and let the kernel apply umask/ACL (this also removes a umask() race between threads), test unixFCmd-21.1.

            ⬜526163ffff2002tty not reset on exitREPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.4); intended since TIP #35

            Open ticket 526163ffff · 25. Channel System · filed 2002-03-05

            Full verdict

            REPRODUCED (main, 9.0, 8.6, 8.4); intended since TIP #35

            • Platform unix
            • Tested Python pty harness: open /dev/pts/N r+; exit (also after -mode, -blocking 0) on main, 9.0.5, 8.6.18, 8.4.20. termios of the pty is changed after exit in all of them; file status flags (O_NONBLOCK) are not, since they belong to Tcl's own open file description.
            • Cause unix/tclUnixChan.c:TclpOpenFileChannel calls TtyInit(), which switches the tty to raw (iflag=IGNBRK, oflag=lflag=0, VMIN=1), and only *after* that saves initState. So TtyCloseProc's doReset (TIP #160) only undoes later fconfigure changes, never the raw mode from the open itself. Not restoring at close was intended by TIP #35 (so Tcl can be used like stty), so changing it would change behaviour.
            • Prototype none (behaviour change; saving initState before TtyInit would also change what -inputmode reset and close restore)
            • Suggested ticket comment Still the case: opening a tty applies TtyInit (raw mode) before initState is saved, so neither close nor -inputmode reset brings back the state from before the open. Keeping settings after close is what TIP #35 wanted. Restoring the state from before the open needs a decision (maybe a TIP).

            • Tested OpenIndiana, main installed with --prefix (runpath, so LD_LIBRARY_PATH is not needed under set-id). Script: #!/bin/sh, set top 1 ;# \, exec .../tclsh9.1 "$0" ${1+"$@"}, then puts "script=[info script] top=[info exists top]". Root was used only to give the script group other (setgid to one's own group does not trigger /dev/fd), then mode 2755. Run as the user: Tcl gets /dev/fd/3 as the script. Unpatched main prints top=0, i.e. it starts reading after the shell's exec line, with both /bin/sh (ksh93) and bash. With the prototype it prints top=1. The ticket's visible error needs a shell that leaves the offset mid-line; ksh93 and bash seek back to the end of the line they consumed, so the remaining text still parses, but the script still runs from the wrong offset. Without set-id both builds read from the start.
            • Cause illumos runs set-id scripts as /dev/fd/N, which shares the offset the shell advanced; generic/tclIOUtil.c:Tcl_FSEvalFileEx/TclNREvalFile never rewind.

            • Suggested ticket comment Reproduced on OpenIndiana: a setgid script is run as /dev/fd/3, and Tcl starts reading at the shell's offset (after the exec line), not at the top. Proposed fix: seek to 0 after opening the script (failure ignored), verified there.
